cards.notes:
- **Filter rows are stored in `conditions[]`.** The builder saves every filled row as `{operator, field, value, title, type, id}` in the trigger's `conditions[]` (`field` and `id` = the asset filter's `field`, `title` = its title, `type` = its `fieldType`) and drops empty rows. It never writes a root `filters` key. [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/Triggers/TriggerMain.ts:888-903; models/Triggers/Filters/MarketplaceFilter.ts:717-722, 1508-1516]
- `masterType` is null in the assets registry; the builder does not copy it. Because this asset carries `workflowsTriggerType: "INTERNAL"`, picking it sets `masterType: "internal"` and save stamps `workflowsTriggerType: "INTERNAL"` on the trigger. (An asset without a `workflowsTriggerType` gets `masterType: "marketplace"` and save stamps its `version` + `templateId` instead.) Save also writes `testResponse`, and `integrationAccountId` when one is set. [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/Triggers/TriggerMain.ts:565-573, 907-908, 921-929]
- Delivery is webhook-based — GHL registers an outbound webhook on the upstream app at activation and tears it down on deactivation. The trigger only fires while the workflow is published and the upstream connection is healthy.
- One or more filter options resolve dynamically (`dynamicSource` or `fetchOptions`). The builder UI fetches option lists at edit-time using the connected app's OAuth token; when constructing the body via API you supply the resolved `value` directly (the server doesn't re-validate against the upstream).

cards.title: add_appointment_booking_ai_bot
cards.summary: Hand the contact off to an AI bot that books an appointment on a specified calendar via conversational flow.

meta.Hybrid / multi-path?: Linear step. When it is saved as the last step of its path, the builder auto-appends an If/Else named `AI Condition` with branches `Did the bot book the appointment?` and `Did the bot time out?` [source-derived 2026-09-29 — components/AsideSection.vue:1931-1933; states/workflow.ts:1698-1771]. Its outcome is branchable downstream: an If/Else condition `ai_bot_booked_appointment` with values `true` ("Booked Appointment"), `false` ("Not booked Appointment"), `timeout` ("Got timed out"). The condition is offered only on the Agency Pro plan and is disabled unless this bot step sits upstream in the same branch family [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/conditions/Condition.ts:1165-1181,1345-1346,1382-1386; utils/ifelse_conditions.ts:417-420].
meta.Premium / beta?: Not flagged in the action registry, but the drawer is gated on the Agency Pro plan: below it the form and Save are hidden and an upgrade notice shows instead [proven-live 2026-09-30 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-W37-walk-add_appointment_booking_ai_bot-main.json; source-derived — components/actions/AddAIAppointmentBot.vue:2,169-170,395-405; states/app.ts:837-845].

cards.validator:
`aiAppointmentBookValidator` (per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json`):

- `calendar_id` set, else `ai_appointment_calendar_required`.
- `timeout_time` set, else `ai_appointment_timeout_required`.
- If `send_first_message`: requires either `template_id` or non-empty `first_message`; if `first_message` is set, must pass `isValidHandleBar` else `ai_appointment_message_invalid_vars`.
- If `no_confirmation_message && send_success_message`: requires either `success_message_template_id` or non-empty `success_message`; handlebar validity check applies the same way.

Per `validators-summary.json`: 4+ fields referenced; result level `warning`.
cards.notes:
- `template_id` and `first_message` are mutually-exclusive alternates — validator accepts either but doesn't error if both are set; behavior in that case unverified.
- `isValidHandleBar` is a lexical check (well-formed `{{ }}` tags), not a resolution check.
- `timeout_time` is in hours: `24` = one day. A value written as seconds or minutes (e.g. `600`) keeps the bot running for 25 days.
- To act on the outcome, add an If/Else after this step with the `ai_bot_booked_appointment` condition (`true` / `false` / `timeout`); Agency Pro plan only.
- The bot's conversation runs server-side via the Eliza service (see `reference/microservices.md` if present); workflow continues only after the bot exits.

cards.title: add_contact_tag
cards.summary: Apply one or more tags to the running contact.

fields.name: type
fields.notes: Class is shared; `type` selects direction. The step-row's top-level `type: "add_contact_tag"` is the source of truth.

fields.name: tags
fields.notes: Tag strings (case-insensitive in storage). 100% of corpus.

fields.name: removeAll
fields.notes: Used by `remove_contact_tag` only. Always omitted on adds.

fields.name: customTags
fields.notes: The "Dynamic" input mode (the picker's Standard / Dynamic switch): one text value, typed or built with the custom-variable picker (merge tags / custom values). Saving in Dynamic mode empties `tags`; saving in Standard mode unsets `customTags`. A step with `customTags` and no `tags` reopens in Dynamic mode `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/ContactTag.ts:29-33,50-55; components/dynamic/TagSelectV2.vue:36-47; components/dynamic/CustomValuePicker.vue:46-50]`.

cards.validator:
`contactTagValidator` (length 213, result level `warning`). Per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json::contactTagValidator`:

```
if (!removeAll && (!tags || tags.length === 0) && !customTags) push { field: "tags", message: "at_least_one_tag_required" }
```

`fields_referenced: ["tags"]`. The validator is satisfied by **any** of:

- non-empty `tags[]`
- non-empty `customTags` string
- `removeAll: true` (only meaningful for `remove_contact_tag`)

For `add_contact_tag` specifically, `removeAll` has no semantic role — `tags` (or `customTags`) is effectively required.
cards.notes:
- **Dynamic mode resolves merge tags per contact** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`: `customTags: "tcwf-3a-dyn-{{contact.last_name}}"` with `tags: []` added the tag with the contact's last name substituted and lower-cased; the standard `tags[]` form added both tags in one step `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3A-crm-basics.json`.
- **Tags are strings, not ids.** The runtime treats `"sba"` and `"SBA"` as the same tag (case-insensitive). Whitespace is significant.
- **`customTags` is the "Dynamic" (custom-value / merge-tag) input mode**, not a multi-select: one text value, and the builder keeps only one of `tags` / `customTags` on save `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/ContactTag.ts:50-55]`. How the runtime splits a resolved value into several tags is not established.
- **New tags typed in the Standard picker are lowercased and created at once** with `POST /{locationId}/tags/create` (`{ tag }`), before the step is saved `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — components/dynamic/TagSelectV2.vue:196-208; services/TagService.ts:9-12]`.
- **No existence check.** Sending a brand-new tag string creates the tag on-the-fly when the action runs.
- **Class is shared with `remove_contact_tag`** — same model file, same validator. The step's top-level `type` is what determines direction at runtime.

cards.title: add_to_workflow
cards.summary: Enroll the running contact into another published workflow.

fields.name: workflow_id
fields.notes: UUID of the destination workflow (the workflow's own id, **not** a `workflow_id` from the trigger envelope). 100%.

fields.name: input_trigger_params
fields.notes: Whether to forward inbound webhook params to the destination workflow. 100%, almost always `false`.

cards.validator:
`addToWorkflowValidator` (length 208, result level `warning`). Per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json::addToWorkflowValidator`:

```
if (!workflow_id || !workflow_id.trim()) push { field: "workflow_id", message: "workflow_selection_required" }
```

`fields_referenced: ["workflow_id"]`. No existence lookup — the validator only checks the string is non-empty. The publish endpoint does not appear to verify the target workflow exists; sending a bogus UUID will publish.
cards.notes:
- **Both `input_trigger_params` values run** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`: with `false` and with `true` the contact was enrolled in the target workflow and its step ran (the target read `finished`); with no inbound-webhook trigger upstream, `true` has nothing to forward and changes nothing visible `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3A-crm-basics.json`.
- **`workflow_id` is the destination workflow's UUID.** This is the workflow's own id (the value in the body's `_id` / `id`), not a trigger id. Sourcing this means making a separate `GET /workflows/{loc}` call to list workflows.
- **No existence check in the validator.** A non-existent target workflow id publishes cleanly — the failure surfaces only at runtime. Verify the target exists before relying on it.
- **`input_trigger_params: true` is for inbound-webhook chaining.** When set, the parent workflow's trigger params (e.g. JSON body fields) are passed into the destination workflow's scope.
- **The destination must be published** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3AR-goal-opp-esd-atw.json`, `live-3AR2-step-log-details.json`: into a published target the step logged `success` ("Started Workflow <name> for contact …") and the target's step ran; into a DRAFT target the step logged `skipped`, `skippedFor: {type: "invalid-data", msg: "Workflow <name> is in Draft mode."}`, and nothing ran there. Publish still accepts a draft target, so the failure shows only in the run log. The log's attributes spell the keys `workflowId` / `inputTriggerParams` (camelCase); the stored step uses `workflow_id` / `input_trigger_params`.
- **No loop guard.** Workflow A can add to workflow B, which can add back to A. Be careful with bidirectional enrollment.

fields.name: prompt
fields.notes: The agent's instructions ("Instructions" in the drawer). The drawer edits them in a rich-text editor and stores **Markdown** (trimmed); merge tags `{{…}}` go in through its custom-value picker [source-derived 2026-09-29 — components/actions/ai-agent-components/AgentPromptEditor.vue:260,439]. A plain-text prompt written by API is read as Markdown [ASSUMPTION — from the editor's Markdown serialiser; runtime not tested].

fields.name: model
fields.notes: Model id from the location's catalog, `GET {baseURL}/agent/{locationId}/models` → `{models[], defaultModelId}`. Each catalog row carries `id`, `displayName`, `provider`, `reasoningLevel`, `recommended`, `contextWindow`, `supportsTools`, `supportsStructuredOutput`, `deprecated`, `fallbackModelId`. Reasoning variants are separate ids with a `_*_low` / `_*_high` suffix (e.g. `gpt-6-luna_*_high`). A new step is seeded with `gpt-6-luna` (an empty saved model is also filled with it); when the catalog loads, a seeded (not user-picked) model is replaced by the location's `defaultModelId`. cards.validator:
`appointmentValidator` checks the following fields (warning-level results) per `sniffs/bundle/trigger-validators-summary.json::appointmentValidator`:

- `appointment.assignedUserId`
- `calendar.id`

All other fields and the body envelope pass without validator inspection. A trigger with no filters is accepted at create time. A filter row with no value is accepted by the API too, but the builder blocks SAVING a trigger that carries one (`TriggerMain.hasErrors` → `checkForEmptyFilter`, `TriggerMain.ts:306-360`; exempt: operator `has-changed`, `has_value`, `has_no_value`, and a value of `false` or `0`) `[source-derived]` — the publish flow uses the same validator chain (`docs/08-validators.md`).
cards.notes:
- 🔴 **A Conversation AI booking reaches this trigger as `appointment.modifiedBy = "user"`, not `customer`.** A "Created By: customer" filter therefore skips every bot booking. To the trigger, a bot booking looks like a staff booking. The appointment record itself says `createdBy: {source: "conversations_ai", userId: null}` (an API create says `third_party`), but no trigger filter reads that field `[proven-live 2026-09-25, trigger log actualValue "user"]`.
- `appointmentValidator` issues a warning when `appointment.assignedUserId` or `calendar.id` reference IDs not in the target location. Per `sniffs/bundle/trigger-validators-summary.json::appointmentValidator`.
- Has two UI configs (`appointmentGuestUIConfig` and `customerAppointmentGuestUIConfig`) for handling guest-vs-customer appointment variations. Per `sniffs/bundle/og-trigger-filters-from-sourcemap.json::AppointmentFilter::ui_configs`.

cards.title: array_functions
cards.summary: Apply an array operation (find, filter, math, line-item construction, find-by-index) to a source array. The README also references this as `array_formatter`.

fields.name: line_items
fields.notes: Build line-item objects from a source array.

cards.validator:
`arrayFunctionsValidator` (per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json`):

- `attributes.action` must be set, else `array_action_required`.
- `action === "find"`: requires `find.fromField` and non-empty `find.filters`.
- `action === "filter"`: requires `filter.fromField` and non-empty `filter.filters`.
- (`math_functions`, `find_by_index`, `line_items` branches not exhaustively shown above; the validator source is truncated in extracted output — open `sniffs/bundle/validators.json::arrayFunctionsValidator` for the full chain.)

Per `validators-summary.json`: 11 fields referenced; result level `warning`. `required_fields_per_validator` includes all sub-action keys.
cards.notes:
- **All six actions proven live** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3H-code-arrays.json` on a custom_code array `[{name:a,n:1},{name:b,n:2},{name:c,n:5}]` (`fromField: "{{custom_code.1.output.items}}"`): `find` (filters `[{key:"name",value:"b"}]`) → the item, read as `{{array_functions.N.<key>}}` (`.n` = `2`); `filter` (name = c) → `{{array_functions.N.result}}` = the matching items ARRAY; `math_functions` (key `n`, all five operations) → `.sum` 8, `.min` 1, `.max` 5, `.average` 2.67 (rounded to 2 dp), `.count` 3; `find_by_index` (index 2) → the THIRD item (0-based), `.name` = `c`; `line_items` (`fields: [{key:"name",value:"name"},{key:"price",value:"n"}]`) → `.result` = the remapped array (`[{name,price}]`); `format_as_text` (`detailField: "name"`, `displayFormat: "custom_separator"`, `customSeparator: " | "`) → `.result` = `a | b | c`. The other three formats `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` (`live-3H2-format-as-text.json`): `comma_separated` → `a, b, c`; `bulleted_list` → `• a` / `• b` / `• c` on separate lines; `numbered_list` → `1. a` / `2. b` / `3. c` on separate lines.
- 🔴 **An array/object `.result` renders as `[object Object]` inside text** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3H-code-arrays.json`: `filter` and `line_items` results written into a text field came out `[object Object]` (one per item). Use `format_as_text` (or `find` + a key) to put array content into text; pass `.result` only to steps that take a list.
- Sub-action discriminator (`action`) toggles which sub-object must be populated. Populating multiple (e.g. both `find` and `filter`) likely no-ops the unused ones — not verified.
- `selectedArray` appears to be runtime-computed state, not user-set — leaving it `[]` should be safe on initial save.
- `line_items` action is used for building invoice/order line-item arrays from raw contact-data arrays.
- The README refers to this as `array_formatter` in some places; the actual type discriminator is `array_functions`.

cards.title: Assign To User
cards.summary: Assign a user to contact
proven: **Live 2026-09-28** `[proven-live]`: `{user_list: [A], only_unassigned_contact: false}` set `assignedTo` A. With `only_unassigned_contact: true` and user B, a contact already owned by A was left alone: the log shows `skipped`, `Contact … is already assigned and action only allows to assign un-assigned contacts`, which is a skip, not an error. An unassigned control got B (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3BV-r2-contact-msteps.json`).

cards.title: assign_user
cards.summary: Assign the contact to one or more users from a list, optionally with traffic-split weights or via a handlebar-resolved user ID.

fields.name: only_unassigned_contact
fields.notes: Skip if the contact is already assigned.

fields.name: total_index
fields.notes: Sum of the normalised weights; the builder computes it on save (`setTrafficIndex`) `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/AssignToUser.ts:71-111]`.

fields.name: traffic_split
fields.notes: `'equally'` | `'unevenly'` ("Equally" / "Unevenly"). The picker shows only when 2 or more users are picked from the standard list `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/AssignToUser.ts:5; components/actions/crm/AssignToUser.vue:224-236; i18n 3104-3105]`.

fields.name: traffic_weightage
fields.notes: `{ [userId]: number }`. With `'unevenly'` each weight is a stepper with min 1; a 0 weight blocks save. With `'equally'` (or one user) the builder rewrites every weight to 1 on save `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — components/actions/crm/AssignToUser.vue:118; models/actions/AssignToUser.ts:72-77,141-143,149-154]`.

fields.name: traffic_index
fields.notes: `{ id: userId, indexes: number[] }[]` — each user's slots out of `total_index`, computed by the builder on save from the weights `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/AssignToUser.ts:9-12,86-109]`.

fields.name: user_list
fields.notes: Static list of user IDs to rotate among.

fields.name: customUserList
fields.notes: Custom-value mode: a `{{handlebar}}` or text resolving to `"userId-1"`, `["userId-1","userId-2"]` or `"userId-1, userId-2"`. Several users are split equally by default. Saving in custom mode empties `user_list`; saving in standard mode unsets `customUserList` `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — i18n 3101-3102; models/actions/AssignToUser.ts:117-124]`.

cards.validator:
`assignToUserValidator` (per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json`):

- If `user_list.length === 0` **AND** `customUserList` is unset, emits `user_list_required` warning.
- For each user ID in `user_list`, emits a `resource: "user"` warning so the resolver verifies the user still exists in the location.

Per `validators-summary.json`: 5 fields referenced; result level `warning`.
cards.notes:
- **`customUserList` resolves a merge tag at run time** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`: `user_list: []`, `customUserList: "{{contact.<text field>}}"` holding a user id assigned that user `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3B-fields-math.json`.
- **`only_unassigned_contact: true` leaves an assigned contact alone** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`: a contact already assigned to user A ran a step assigning user B with the switch on and still read A `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3A-crm-basics.json`.

- **`unevenly` splits by weight at run time, with or without the builder's index** `[proven-live 2026-09-26]`: weights 3/1 over two users, 4 run-created contacts in sequence → assignments A, A, A, B — both for a step authored through the API (stored `total_index: 0`, `traffic_index: []`) and for one carrying the builder-computed `total_index: 4`, `traffic_index: [{A:[1,2,3]},{B:[4]}]` (`setTrafficIndex`, `models/actions/AssignToUser.ts:69-111`). The runtime derives the rotation from `user_list` + `traffic_weightage`; the two index fields are builder bookkeeping. Each run logs `contact got assigned to user with id: …` (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-D-assign-uneven.json`; test users only, never real ones).
- `customUserList` accepts a handlebar that must resolve to a valid user ID at run time; no validator pre-flight on the handlebar contents.
- `traffic_index` and `total_index` are derived from `traffic_weightage` by the builder on save, not runtime counters. An API-built step should store what the builder would compute (for 2 users weighted 1:1 → `total_index: 2`, `traffic_index: [{id:A,indexes:[1]},{id:B,indexes:[2]}]`) `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/AssignToUser.ts:71-111]`.
- `only_unassigned_contact: true` short-circuits the rotation when the contact already has an `assignedTo` — no rotation advance, no new assignment.
- For weighted distribution set `traffic_split: "unevenly"` and `traffic_weightage: { [userId]: weight }` with every weight ≥ 1 (the enum has no `"weighted"` value) `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/AssignToUser.ts:5; components/actions/crm/AssignToUser.vue:118]`.

cards.title: call
cards.summary: Place an outbound call to the contact, optionally with a whisper message for the agent.

fields.name: timeout
fields.notes: "Call timeout (s)". Range **1–600** seconds; `0` has its own error ("Timeout with value 0 is not allowed") `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/Call.ts:3-4,16; components/actions/call-timeout-validation.ts:9-25; utils/validators/communication-validators.ts:20-36; i18n 856,862,6120]`.

fields.name: whisper_message
fields.notes: "The message you want the person who answers the phone to hear" — played three times before the call connects; custom variables allowed `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/Call.ts:17; components/actions/Call.vue:19-48; i18n 858]`.

fields.name: disable_detect_voicemail
fields.notes: If true, skip voicemail detection (removes the connect delay). Interacts with Stop On Reply: with detection on, a voicemail answer lets the contact continue; with detection off, the workflow stops when either a person or a voicemail answers. The builder recommends a timeout under 20 s when it is off `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/Call.ts:18; components/actions/Call.vue:85-100; i18n 859-861]`.

fields.name: call_connect
fields.notes: "Connect Call after Keypress". Tooltip: disable only if the call doesn't connect after the key press; it auto-connects after playing the whisper three times. A stored step without the key is back-filled to `true` when opened `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/Call.ts:19,28-31; components/actions/Call.vue:102-114; i18n 3907-3908]`.

cards.validator:
`callValidator` (per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json`):

- `timeout` must be set and `> 0`, else `timeout_required` warning.
- If set, must satisfy `1 <= timeout <= 600`, else `timeout_must_be_between_1_and_600` warning `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/validators/communication-validators.ts:28-35]`.

Per `validators-summary.json`: 1 field referenced; result level `warning`.
cards.notes:
- `timeout: 600` is stored as authored and read back unchanged `[proven-live 2026-09-26]`. Run on a contact with no phone, the step logs `status: skipped`, `skippedFor: {type: "missing-data", msg: "No Phone number"}` and the workflow continues to the next step (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-B-semantics.json`).
- All three options are stored as authored: `whisper_message` with a merge tag, `disable_detect_voicemail: true`, `call_connect: false` (with `timeout: 20`), read back unchanged `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3AT-call-options.json`). What they do on a real call (whisper played, voicemail detection, keypress connect) needs a placed call and is not measured.
- `attributes.type` is **not** in the corpus example — unusual for an OG action. Server may default it from the step-level `type`. Other steps include both.
- The 1–600 second timeout range `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/Call.ts:3-4]` is enforced only as a warning by the validator; the builder drawer refuses to save outside it (`hasErrors` → `isTimeoutWithinLimit`, `models/actions/Call.ts:69-79`).
- "Call" here is the auto-dialer/IVR-style action; for click-to-call by a user, see [`manual-call`](./manual-call.md).

fields.name: model
fields.notes: OpenAI model id. The picker offers 9: `gpt-6-luna` and `gpt-6-sol` (both flagged new, listed first), `gpt-5`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5-nano`, `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4-turbo`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-5.1`. A new step is seeded with `gpt-6-luna`, and a saved step with an empty `model` is filled with it. Deprecated ids are rewritten on load: `gpt-4-turbo-preview` → `gpt-4-turbo`, `gpt-3.5-turbo` → `gpt-4o-mini` [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/premium-actions/ChatGPT.ts:40-52,72-118,242-248,258,280]. 100%.

fields.name: actionType
fields.notes: Drawer mode: picks the `actionParams` inputs and the template that builds `promptText` (see Notes). The picker offers four: `classify_text` is listed as "Classify Text (Coming Soon)" and disabled, and no drawer input writes `actionParams.categories`, so `classify_text` is API-only [source-derived 2026-09-29 — models/actions/premium-actions/ChatGPT.ts:151-183; chatgpt-components/ActionParams.vue:1-91]. All five ran on `gpt-5-nano` when written by API [proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3P-chatgpt.json]. 100%.

fields.name: actionParams
fields.notes: Mode-specific params. `{ message, categories, length, from, to, memoryKeyToggle, memoryKeyType, memoryKeyCustom }`. **Editor state only**: the runtime answers `promptText`, not these [proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3P-chatgpt.json, step 6]. 100%.

fields.name: actionParams.message
fields.notes: Validator references it; required when `actionType` demands it.

fields.name: memoryKey
fields.notes: Key for chat-history persistence between calls. A new step is seeded `""` with `memoryKeyToggle: false`; on save the drawer writes `""` when the toggle is off, else `location` / `workflow` / `workflow_status` / `action`, or `memoryKeyCustom` for `custom` [source-derived 2026-09-28 — models/actions/premium-actions/ChatGPT.ts:216-241,272,486-510]. 100%.

fields.name: excludeFromHistory
fields.notes: Skip storing this turn in memory. 100%.

fields.name: apiKey
fields.notes: Seeded empty. The drawer has no API-key input ("Hide Model and APIKey as we'll use our default values"), so the UI never sets it [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/premium-actions/ChatGPT.ts:61-63,256,278]. 100%.

cards.validator:
`chatGPTValidator` (length 1456, result level `warning`). Per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json::chatGPTValidator`:

1. `promptText` non-empty, AND passes `isValidHandleBar` (Handlebars syntax valid).
2. `temperature` non-empty, parses to a number in `[0, 1]`.
3. `event` set.
4. Conditional checks on `actionParams` by `actionType` (the drawer's `isValidActionParams`): `translate_content` needs `message`, `from` and `to`; `summarize_text` needs `message` and `length`; `analyze_text_sentiment` needs `message`; `classify_text` and `custom` need none [source-derived 2026-09-28 — models/actions/premium-actions/ChatGPT.ts:352-368].

`fields_referenced` (7): `actionParams.from`, `actionParams.length`, `actionParams.message`, `actionParams.to`, `event`, `promptText`, `temperature`.
cards.notes:
- **`temperature` is stored as a string**, not a number. `"0.2"` works; `0.2` (number) may also work but corpus shows the string form exclusively.
- **`model` defaults to `"gpt-6-luna"`** for a new step, and an empty `model` on an existing step is filled with it (it was `gpt-5-mini` in the 2026-09-18 builder). The corpus examples carry `"gpt-5"`, which is still a selectable id [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/premium-actions/ChatGPT.ts:258,280].
- **`event: "simple-prompt"` is the only value.** It is the single entry in the drawer's event options, and the event selector is not shown [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/premium-actions/ChatGPT.ts:59,66-71].
- **`promptText` Handlebars validation is strict.** Invalid Handlebars (e.g. unclosed `{{`) trips the validator. Empty prompt does too.
- **Downstream access** is via `{{chatgpt.<N>.response}}`, where N is the step's per-type `stepIndex` (1 for the first chatgpt step, 2 for the second…). Six chatgpt steps in one workflow rendered as `{{chatgpt.1.response}}`…`{{chatgpt.6.response}}` in a later field write [proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3P-chatgpt.json]. The response is the raw model text, extra lines included (a translation came back with an added usage note). Compound paths like `{{chatgpt.4.response.<key>}}` exist when the response is structured (e.g. JSON mode).
- **`memoryKey`** scopes the chat history. With `memoryKeyType: "action"` it's per-action-per-contact; `"custom"` lets you scope by an arbitrary key (e.g. group multiple steps into one conversation). Measured: two steps sharing `memoryKey: "workflow_status"` in one run — the first planted a code word, the second recalled it; a third step with `memoryKey: ""` asked the same question and answered NONE; two steps sharing a custom key recalled theirs too [proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3P4-chatgpt-memory.json]; two steps sharing `memoryKey: "workflow"` recalled theirs [proven-live 2026-09-28 — live-3P5-chatgpt-memory2.json]. `location` and `action` are the same key mechanism and were not run (`location` would write memory other workflows' steps may read; `action` needs a second execution) [inferred from the drawer writing them as plain `memoryKey` strings, ChatGPT.ts:486-510].
- **`excludeFromHistory: true` keeps that turn out of memory.** A step that planted a code word with it on, followed by a step on the same custom key, answered NONE [proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3P5-chatgpt-memory2.json]. `excludeInstructionsFromHistory` was not run.
- **`instructions` is sent as the system prompt.** A step whose `instructions` said "reply with exactly QUINCE" answered QUINCE to the `promptText` "Say hello." [proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3P4-chatgpt-memory.json].
- **`apiKey`**: leave it `""` or omit it. Both runs used GHL's own key and succeeded [proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3P-chatgpt.json (omitted), live-3P2-chatgpt-apikey.json (`""`)]. The builder has no UI for it; whether the runtime honours a non-empty value is untested [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/premium-actions/ChatGPT.ts:61-63].
- **The drawer builds `promptText` from a template per mode**, and an API author must do the same, because the runtime reads only `promptText` [source-derived 2026-09-28 — models/actions/premium-actions/ChatGPT.ts:185-208,410-452; runtime proven-live as above]:
  - `analyze_text_sentiment`: `Just reply only with POSITIVE, if the below message has positive intent and NEGATIVE if the message has negative intent \n\n<message>` → ran `POSITIVE`.
  - `classify_text`: `Categorize the given text into one of the following categories: <categories joined by ", "> \n\n\n      Text: <message>` → ran `billing`.
  - `summarize_text`: `Summarize the following text in <length>. Capture the key points and essential information while remaining concise and faithful to the original.\n\n Text: \n\n<message>` → ran a one-sentence summary.
  - `translate_content`: `Translate the below Text from <from> to <to> Text: \n\n<message>` → ran Spanish.
  - `custom`: the author's own `promptText`. Picking Custom from the Action type dropdown clears it; the pencil icon on a preset mode's read-only Prompt switches to custom and keeps the composed text [source-derived 2026-09-29 — components/actions/premium-actions/ChatGPT.vue:228-232; models/actions/premium-actions/ChatGPT.ts:453-455].
- **Premium gate.** `isPremiumAction: true`. Before rendering, the drawer checks the location's `workflow_ai` plan (`config.optIn`, failing open) and shows a paywall instead of the form when it is off (see Builder options and limits).

cards.title: Clear Associated Company Fields
cards.summary: Clear selected fields of the primary company associated with the contact.
proven: - 🔴 **On a contact with NO company, it FAILS** `[proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3BZ2-r7-contact-company.json]`. The log shows `status: failed`, "Contact does not have a business", in the same run where `update_associated_company` only skipped. A failed step triggers GHL's workflow error notification, which by default emails every agency and location admin (see [`../../50-runtime/error-notifications.md`](../../50-runtime/error-notifications.md)). **Guard it with an If/Else on the contact having a company**, or run it only where every contact has one.

- 🔴 **Accepted, not applied — even with the builder's own row** `[proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3CC-clear-company-reproof.json; live-3BZ2-r7-contact-company.json, live-3BZ2-reread-company.json]`. The builder saves each row as `{"__customInputs__": {}, "filterField": "business.<key>"}` `[proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3CB2-clear-company-builder-row.json, builder drawer captured under a write guard]`. That exact row (website + description) ran on a contact whose company had both fields set. It logged `success`, "Action execution

- 🔴 **The UI promises a skip; the runtime fails** (third failure class) `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`. The step's drawer says "If no company is associated, this action will be skipped." The run on a contact with no company logged `status: failed`, not skipped. Every read of the step agrees with the drawer, but a user reading that sentence expects the opposite of what happens.

cards.title: clear_custom_object_fields
cards.summary: Clear (set to null/empty) one or more fields on an existing custom-object record. Resolved from `!ident:CustomObjectActionTypes.CLEAR_FIELDS`.

fields.name: type
fields.notes: Inner type, equal to the step type.

fields.name: key
fields.notes: The target object's key: `custom_objects.<object>`, or `contact` for an associated contact. Never `business` or `opportunity`.

fields.name: fields
fields.notes: `fieldKey` is the schema field's ID (not its fieldKey). These are the fields to clear; the drawer has no value input and a builder save writes no `value`. At least one row unless `clearOwner` or `clearFollowers` is true. The primary display field is offered only for a CRM target (`contact` / `opportunity`); required fields are offered.

fields.name: makeAssociation
fields.notes: No drawer control; the builder writes `false` on a new step and on every Object change.

fields.name: associations
fields.notes: Association ids from the **Association label** select, or `["all_related_associations"]` for `All associated {objectName}`. Required when the target is not the workflow's own object; also offered for the workflow's own object when it has self-association labels.

cards.validator: No validator registered. Publish enforcement absent at the bundle level.
cards.notes:
- "Clear" semantics (null vs. delete-key vs. empty-string) are not documented in the bundle and have not been server-tested. Likely sets each listed field to null, but verify.
- Distinct from `update_custom_object` with `value: ""` — clear is a separate action type, suggesting different server behavior (e.g. unsetting indices vs. storing empty strings).

It never writes a root `filters` key. [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/Triggers/TriggerMain.ts:888-903; models/Triggers/Filters/MarketplaceFilter.ts:717-722, 1508-1516]
- `masterType` is null in the assets registry; the builder does not copy it. Because this asset carries `workflowsTriggerType: "INTEGRATION_AI"`, picking it sets `masterType: "internal"` and save stamps `workflowsTriggerType: "INTEGRATION_AI"` on the trigger. (An asset without a `workflowsTriggerType` gets `masterType: "marketplace"` and save stamps its `version` + `templateId` instead.) Save also writes `testResponse`, and `integrationAccountId` when one is set. [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/Triggers/TriggerMain.ts:565-573, 907-908, 921-929]
- The trigger is gated behind an OAuth connection to the upstream app (`appId` `68908ee34f9a3b062967cd03`).
- Delivery is webhook-based — GHL registers an outbound webhook on the upstream app at activation and tears it down on deactivation. The trigger only fires while the workflow is published and the upstream connection is healthy.
- Premium trigger (`config.isPremiumTrigger: true`) — gated behind plan tier or labs flag.
- One or more filter options resolve dynamically (`dynamicSource` or `fetchOptions`). The builder UI fetches option lists at edit-time using the connected app's OAuth token; when constructing the body via API you supply the resolved `value` directly (the server doesn't re-validate against the upstream).
- Filters have `dependentFilters` chains (parent → child option fetches). Populate values top-down or the dependent filter's option set is empty.

cards.title: contact_changed
cards.summary: Fires when one or more chosen contact fields are updated.
cards.validator:
`contactChangedValidator` checks the following fields (warning-level results) per `sniffs/bundle/trigger-validators-summary.json::contactChangedValidator`:

- `contact.assignedTo`

All other fields and the body envelope pass without validator inspection. A trigger with no filters is accepted at create time. A filter row with no value is accepted by the API too, but the builder blocks SAVING a trigger that carries one (`TriggerMain.hasErrors` → `checkForEmptyFilter`, `TriggerMain.ts:306-360`; exempt: operator `has-changed`, `has_value`, `has_no_value`, and a value of `false` or `0`) `[source-derived]` — the publish flow uses the same validator chain (`docs/08-validators.md`).
cards.notes: - Most rows use the `has-changed` operator (literal in the TS source) — the trigger fires when the field changed, not just when it equals a value. `contactChangedValidator` warns on missing `contact.assignedTo` when that row is configured.

cards.title: contact_created
cards.summary: Fires the moment a new contact is created in the location.
cards.validator: `contactCreatedValidator` emits a **warning-level** `custom_field` reference check for every `contact.*` row in `conditions[]` except every standard contact field (`getStandardContactFields()`). The builder resolves each against the location's custom fields: an unknown field id gives `contact_custom_field_not_found`, and a picklist value that is not one of the field's options gives `invalid_custom_field_value`. Every finding, warning or error, is pushed into the builder's highlight-error map with no severity filter, and a non-empty map blocks Publish in the builder (a client-side gate). [source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/validators/triggers/contact-validators.ts:56-58; utils/validators/template-validator.ts:740-768; utils/validators/template-validator.ts:188-202; utils/highlight-errors.ts:14-27; hooks/use-publish-gate.ts:95-106]
cards.notes: - `contact.email`, `contact.phone`, and `contact.type` are input/select filter rows. Tag row uses `tagsAdded` field-id (same logical row as `TagFilter::tag_added`). `contactCreatedValidator` runs only the checks listed under `## Validator`.

It never writes a root `filters` key. [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/Triggers/TriggerMain.ts:888-903; models/Triggers/Filters/MarketplaceFilter.ts:717-722, 1508-1516]

Because this asset carries `workflowsTriggerType: "INTERNAL"`, picking it sets `masterType: "internal"` and save stamps `workflowsTriggerType: "INTERNAL"` on the trigger. (An asset without a `workflowsTriggerType` gets `masterType: "marketplace"` and save stamps its `version` + `templateId` instead.) The builder resolves each against the location's custom fields: an unknown field id gives `contact_custom_field_not_found`, and a picklist value that is not one of the field's options gives `invalid_custom_field_value`. Every finding, warning or error, is pushed into the builder's highlight-error map with no severity filter, and a non-empty map blocks Publish in the builder (a client-side gate). cards.title: conv_ai_trigger
cards.summary: Fires when a conversation AI bot session starts for a contact.

fields.name: botId
fields.notes: `operator: "=="`, `type: "input"`, `title: ""`. Renders **disabled** once the flow is bound.

filterRows.title: Select Conversation AI bot
filterRows.notes: `operator: "=="`, `type: "input"`, `title: ""`. Renders **disabled** once the flow is bound.

cards.validator: None bound in TriggerMaster — picker uses runtime defaults. Per `sniffs/bundle/trigger-registry-parsed.json::entries[]` for `conv_ai_trigger`, the `validation.code` slot is empty.
cards.notes:
- Carries `inCompatibleActions()`, `recommendedActions()`, and `uiControls.disable()` functions in the registry — the builder uses these to filter the action picker and gate adding duplicate conv-AI triggers. Per `DISCOVERIES.md §15`.
- Conditions use a `botId` field as a free-text input (not a filter row from a TS model). Per `catalog/trigger-examples/conv_ai_trigger.json`.
- **The API enforces none of the builder's immutability.** The flow builder makes this trigger uneditable and the workflow undeletable; the API does not. Live-proven 2026-08-26, one attempt each, each read back separately: `PUT` with a different `botId` → 200, applied (the flow now belongs to another agent); `PUT` with `type: "contact_tag"` → 200, applied, conditions wiped. Only DELETE is refused, with `403 Workflows with type "agent" cannot be deleted`. Breaking either half orphans the bot — it keeps `objectiveBuilderWorkflowId` while nothing can enter the flow. The engine therefore refuses `modifyTrigger`/`deleteTrigger` on a `conv_ai_trigger` itself (hatch: `ctx.allowFlowTriggerEdit`).
- **Flow workflows report `status: "published"`** on creation, whether engine-built or UI-built, while non-flow workflows on the same account stay `draft`. The draft-first guarantee does not hold for `workflowType: "agent"`. [proven-live — observed on every flow workflow on the test account] The builder side matches: a workflow holding a `conv_ai_trigger` is **locked to published** — the status toggle is disabled (tooltip "Workflows with Agent Triggers must always be published"), because drafting one would orphan in-flight AI conversations. [source-derived 2026-09-26 — components/workflow-page-header/WorkflowStatusToggle.vue:7-21, 64-81]
- **A flow can only be entered by this trigger, and can only gain custom triggers.** `uiControls.hideOtherTriggers` filters the whole trigger picker down to `conv_ai_autonomous_trigger` once a `conv_ai_trigger` exists — so a flow workflow can never gain an ordinary trigger, only up to 3 [`Custom triggers`](./conv_ai_autonomous_trigger.md). Confirmed live: with the plan state resolved, "Add new trigger" shows exactly one option, "Custom trigger".
- **Not supported in the Advanced Builder.** `uiControls.disable` returns *"Conversation AI trigger is not supported in Advanced Builder"* when the advanced canvas is active. This matters on accounts that default to it.
- **Only one per workflow, and it cannot share a workflow with any other trigger type** — *"conv_ai_trigger_already_exists_in_workflow"* / *"cannot_add_conv_ai_trigger_with_other_triggers"*.
- **It cannot be added to an already-existing workflow.** If `workflow.version > 1` the builder refuses with *"conv_ai_trigger_cant_be_added_to_already_existing_workflow"* — a flow must be a flow from creation. [source-derived — from `uiControls.disable`; not tested against the API, which enforces none of the other rules on this surface]

cards.title: AI message
cards.summary: Have the bot compose and send a message from an instruction, in its own words.

fields.name: message
fields.notes: placeholder `Input the prompt for the Message`

cards.notes:
- `waitForReply` is **required as a presence**, not as a truth: `false` is accepted and meaningful (send and move on). Omit it entirely and the node renders with an error badge.
- The engine defaults `waitForReply` rather than leaving it for the builder to reject.
- 🔴 **The node's local scope overrides a global prohibition** `[proven-live]`. A contact parked at an AI message node scoped to a narrow job asked, off-script, for something outside that scope, and the reply contained the exact sentences the agent's global prompt banned twice. The node's `message` said nothing wrong — it simply implied a narrower job, and with no positive bridge the model declared incapacity. Repeat behavioural rules in this node's `message`, byte-identically with every other speaking node and with the positive half ("say yes, ask for what you would need"). Re-run with the block appended, the same off-script request was handled correctly. See [flow-bot-runtime-doctrine](../../40-rules/flow-bot-runtime-doctrine.md).

cards.title: AI splitter
cards.summary: Let the model choose a branch from a natural-language description of each one.

fields.name: description
fields.notes: placeholder `Describe the branching logic, e.g., whether the customer owns a house or not`

cards.notes:
- **Multi-path**, plus an automatic `No condition met` fallback branch.
- `description` is required. The engine falls back to the node NAME when it is omitted, and rejects a node that has neither.
- Each authored branch needs a name; an unnamed branch is rejected.
- 🔴 **A branch whose FIRST step is a multipath container is never offered to the model** `[proven-live]`. Wired directly to a `conversationai_book_appointment`, a branch was never chosen across four conversations matching its label almost verbatim — the splitter logged `success` and took the default every time, and two `description` rewrites changed nothing. Insert one simple step (`add_notes`, `add_to_workflow`, `update_contact_field`…) at the head of the branch; the starved branch then fired on the next message. No error surfaces anywhere: the builder shows the branch and the graph round-trips clean. See [flow-bot-runtime-doctrine](../../40-rules/flow-bot-runtime-doctrine.md).
- If the "No condition met" fallback branch ends in a `conversationai_continue`, it cannot act on the diary — that node has no booking tool, however it is worded `[proven-live]`.

cards.title: Book appointment
cards.summary: Hand the conversation to the booking flow for one calendar, then branch on the outcome.

fields.name: promptInstructions
fields.default: Get the customer to book an appointment

cards.notes:
- **Multi-path.** Emits `cat: "multi-path"`, `convertToMultipath: true`, `transitions[]`, and one `type: "transition"` child per branch.
- Branch fields are pre-defined: the first transition carries `{ appointmentBooked: true, appointmentNotBooked: false }`, the second `{ appointmentNotBooked: true }`.
- `calendarId` is required and takes the calendar id. `promptInstructions` is optional and defaults to `Get the customer to book an appointment`.
- 🔴 **Its empty-result wording is hard-coded** `[proven-live]`. When the node finds no appointment for the contact it emits its own refusal ("I can't move or reschedule existing appointments"); five `promptInstructions` strategies failed to change it while a diagnostic instruction ("begin every reply with the word PINEAPPLE") was obeyed — the node honours the *form* of `promptInstructions` and overrides the *content* for this case. Fix is structural: identify the contact first (an objective asking for the email/phone the booking was made under triggers the record merge) and gate the node behind an `if_else` on a booking-live tag so it is only asked about someone who has one.
- **Its appointment SELECTION is steerable** `[proven-live]`. There is no field for *which* appointment; by default it names an already-attended appointment and offers past times, and with several future bookings silently picks the soonest. `promptInstructions` fixes both ("never name or offer a past time; if more than one booking is still to come, say how many and ask which; otherwise use the next one"). Capability vs selection: if the node has ever done the right thing, wording is the lever. See [flow-bot-runtime-doctrine](../../40-rules/flow-bot-runtime-doctrine.md).
- 🔴 **Never place this node as the FIRST step of a splitter branch** — it is a multipath container, and a splitter branch led by a container is never offered to the model `[proven-live]`. Lead the branch with one simple step.

cards.title: Continue conversation
cards.summary: Return the contact to the bot’s general conversation, driven by the global prompt and knowledge base.
cards.notes:
- **TERMINAL.** The builder renders no "Add action" after this node; its edge runs straight to END. Nothing can follow it.
- `instructions` is optional but is **stored even when blank** (`""`). It is not an empty attributes object, as previously documented.
- The panel labels this field ADDITIONAL INSTRUCTIONS; the wire key is `instructions`. The previously documented `prompt` never existed.
- 🔴 **The node has NO appointment tool, and no prompt wording can give it one** `[proven-live]`. From inside a continue node the agent can only talk; it will truthfully deny being able to move, cancel or book anything, whatever the global or local instructions say — five prompt layers were tried and all failed. Instructing it to claim the capability instructs it to lie. Route diary intents to `conversationai_book_appointment`; word this node to keep the conversation alive without a false claim. See [flow-bot-runtime-doctrine](../../40-rules/flow-bot-runtime-doctrine.md).
- A behavioural rule in the global prompt does not reach this node unless repeated in its `instructions`, byte-identically and with a positive half `[proven-live]` — same doctrine page.

cards.title: Custom message

cards.notes:
- Same `waitForReply` presence rule as `conversationai_ai_message`.
- Supports custom variables through the picker; the stored value is the raw template string.

fields.notes: stored and round-trips, but NOT in the marketplace asset’s field list

cards.notes:
- **TERMINAL, and enforced oddly.** An `end` inserted mid-flow appears on the canvas and is then **silently dropped when the workflow saves** — absent from the persisted document, with no error. Reproduced twice on 2026-08-26. Author it last.
- 🔴 **The panel labels do not match the wire keys**, and this is where three wrong names came from: END CUSTOM MESSAGE → `message`, REACTIVATE AFTER BOT → `sleepEnabled`, REACTIVATE AFTER (VALUE) → `sleepDuration`, REACTIVATE AFTER (UNIT) → `sleepUnit`.
- `sleepEnabled` is required and defaults on. Authoring `sleepEnabled: false` opts out and pulls in no schedule.
- `sleepDuration` / `sleepUnit` are not in the asset’s field list but are stored and round-trip through the builder (captured live).

cards.title: AI capture information
cards.summary: Ask the contact for one piece of information and store the answer on a contact field.

fields.name: objective
fields.notes: placeholder `Input the prompt for the objective `

fields.name: responseExample
fields.notes: placeholder `Add responses example that you expect from the customer `

fields.name: proceedIfNotMet
fields.notes: 🔴 INVERTED NAME — this IS "Don't Proceed to Next Objective If Criteria not Met.": `true` BLOCKS, `false` proceeds. `true` makes `closingMessage` required.

cards.notes:
- This is a **premium** node: the stored row carries a numeric `stepIndex` that ordinary nodes do not.
- `maxAttempts` is stored as authored — the asset default is the string `"5"`, and live captures carry the number `2`. Both persist; the builder does not normalise it.
- `contactField` takes the custom field **id**, not its name.
- 🔴 **`proceedIfNotMet` MEANS THE OPPOSITE OF ITS NAME.** The marketplace asset binds it DIRECTLY to a checkbox titled "Don't Proceed to Next
  Objective If Criteria not Met." (`fieldType: checkbox`, no inversion layer), so `true` = the box is
  CHECKED = the objective BLOCKS and keeps asking; `false` = carry on to the next objective. An author
  who means "continue even when the criteria are not met" wants **false**.
- **`true` makes `closingMessage` REQUIRED**, and reveals an optional `tags`. The asset's
  `dynamicFieldsConfig.customGenerator` returns both the moment the field is truthy, with
  `closingMessage` marked `required: true` — it is what the bot says when it gives up on the objective.
  Corroborated by a UI-built capture on a client account: five objectives at `false` carry neither key,
  the one at `true` carries both.
- 🔴 **At runtime, `true` on an unmet objective sends `closingMessage` and ENDS the run** `[proven-live]`. In a lane that ends at a booking node, an undecided lead ("ok, maybe I'll come in then") was judged unmet, got the closing message, and the run finished — a warm close instead of times. Every capture in a booking lane must carry `false`; the closing texts stay (validator-required) but must never gate the lane. See [flow-bot-runtime-doctrine](../../40-rules/flow-bot-runtime-doctrine.md).
- **An objective asking for the email or phone a booking was made under makes GHL merge the anonymous visitor into their existing contact record** `[proven-live]` — the practical way to make a booking findable before a `conversationai_book_appointment`. The merge retires the old conversation id `[proven-live — a harness measurement fault recorded in the certification's Method section: the watcher on the dead id saw messages disappear that had landed on the surviving thread]`.
- A behavioural rule in the global prompt does not reach this node unless repeated in its `instructions`, byte-identically and with a positive half `[proven-live]` — same doctrine page.

cards.title: Services booking
cards.summary: Book a commerce **service** (rather than a calendar) from inside the conversation.

fields.name: conversationai_booking_description

cards.title: create_opportunity
cards.summary: Create or update an opportunity record on a pipeline+stage for the running contact. The builder shows a deprecation banner on this step: "The Create/Update Action will soon be deprecated. Existing Workflows will be unaffected; however, the new Create Opportunity and Update Opportunity actions will b

fields.name: pipeline_id
fields.notes: Pipeline UUID/MongoID. Resolves against the location's pipelines. 100%.

fields.name: pipeline_stage_id
fields.notes: Stage UUID within the pipeline. Validator emits a resource lookup. 96.8%.

fields.name: opportunity_source
fields.notes: Source/attribution label. Empty = unchanged on update, the contact's source on create `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — i18n 3120 `opportunity_source_help_text`]`. 100% (often empty).

fields.name: opportunity_status
fields.default: — (absent until a status is picked; the drawer pre-selects none and Save does not require one)
fields.notes: `"open" | "won" | "lost" | "abandoned"` — all four are the builder's Status options; how the runtime treats an absent status is untested `[ASSUMPTION — source cannot settle it]` `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/Workflow.ts:666-671; models/actions/CreateOpportunity.ts:220-227]`. 80.6%.

fields.name: monetary_value
fields.notes: Stored as string, parsed at execution. 100%.

fields.name: allow_backward
fields.notes: If true, allow moving the opp to an earlier stage. Cannot be on together with `allow_multiple`: the builder refuses the second toggle with a modal ("will always create a new Opportunity" vs "only work when an Opportunity already exists") `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — components/actions/crm/CreateOpportunity.vue:275-299]`. 16.1%.

fields.name: allow_multiple
fields.notes: Set to `true` to always create a new card, never reuse the contact's existing one in this pipeline `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`. Absent = upsert (below).

fields.name: fields
fields.notes: Custom-field writes on the opportunity. 96.8% (mostly empty).

cards.notes:
- **`abandoned` is a current status** `[proven-live 2026-09-26]`: a step with `opportunity_status: "abandoned"` created a card whose read-back status is `abandoned`. The step stores **snake_case** `pipeline_id` / `pipeline_stage_id` / `opportunity_status` / `opportunity_name` (read back on a separate request) (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-C-opportunity.json`).
- 🔴 **This step does not bind its card to the run** `[proven-live 2026-09-26]`: an If/Else on `opportunities` / `pipelineStageId` placed after it read ELSE although the card had just been created in that stage — immediately, after a 1-minute wait, and for an `abandoned` card alike (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-C3-opp-condition.json`). Positive control: the SAME condition after a `find_opportunity` (Found branch) took the stage branch for a contact holding a card in that stage (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-C4-opp-control.json`). The update side agrees: an `internal_update_opportunity` (status won) right after this step logged `skipped` "Internal Action Error - Please use Opportunity trigger/find opportunity action to get the opportunity" and the card stayed `open`, while the same update after [`internal_create_opportunity`](./internal_create_opportunity.md) wrote the card (`won`) (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-W24-create-binds.json`) `[proven-live 2026-09-26]`. So an opportunity branch or update after this step needs a `find_opportunity` in front of it, or use `internal_create_opportunity` when the next step must act on the new card.
- **`create_opportunity` actually updates** if the contact already has an opportunity in the same pipeline — an open one, and a **lost** one too: it reopens that card and overwrites its stage, name and value. Only `allow_multiple: true` creates a second card `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`. Proven by runtime differential, not inferred from the registry's display name — see below. The "create vs update" decision happens at runtime; this step doesn't expose a discriminator.
- **`pipeline_id` format varies.** Older pipelines use MongoIDs (e.g. `"PIPELINE_ID"`), newer use UUIDs. The validator accepts both — the publish endpoint's `resource: "pipeline"` lookup resolves either.
- **`pipeline_stage_id` is UUID-format** even when the pipeline is MongoID-format. Two different id stores.
- **`opportunity_status: "abandoned"` is a current value**, one of the four in the builder's Status enum and offered in the status picker `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/Workflow.ts:666-671; models/actions/CreateOpportunity.ts:220-227]`.
- **Deprecated in the builder.** The step carries a banner saying Create/Update "will soon be deprecated", replaced by Create Opportunity and Update Opportunity; existing workflows are unaffected `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — components/actions/crm/CreateOpportunity.vue:6; i18n 5176]`. Which step types those two are is not named in the banner.
- **`monetary_value` is a string, not a number.** Stored as `""` or `"123.45"`. Handlebars work here.
- For internal/AI-driven creation, see [`internal_create_opportunity`](./internal_create_opportunity.md) (different attribute shape).

cards.title: create_update_contact
cards.summary: Create a contact (or update if one matches on email/phone) by writing one or more field values.

fields.name: fields
fields.notes: Per-field write rows; see sub-table below. Validator requires `length > 0`.

cards.validator:
`createUpdateContactValidator` (per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json`):

- `attributes.fields.length > 0` else `at_least_one_field_required`.
- For each row: `field` must be set; `value` must be set unless `date === "currentDate"` or value is literally `false`/`0`.
- At least one row's `field` must be `"email"` or `"phone"` (the contact identity lookup keys).
- Non-standard `field` values trigger a `custom_field` resource warning (resolved by `06-fields-glossary.md`).

Per `validators-summary.json`: 14 fields referenced; result level `warning`.
cards.notes:
- **In a contact-LESS run it creates, then updates by email** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3J-webhook-chain.json`, `live-3J-webhook-chain-logs-late.json`: an inbound-webhook run with no contact created a contact from the payload's email/first/last name; a second POST with the SAME email updated that contact's last name (same id — no duplicate). The run's enrolment then belongs to that contact. Once a run holds a contact (from its trigger, an enrolment, or a `find_contact` Found) the step is skipped — `live-3J2-find-contactless.json`.
- 🔴 **Skipped in any run that already has a contact** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3G-contacts.json`: enrolled with a contact, the step logs `skipped`, `skippedFor: {type: "missing-data", msg: "Only one contact is allowed per workflow, and <contact name> is already in use."}` and does nothing. No contact was created or updated. It is for runs that start WITHOUT a contact (e.g. an inbound-webhook or scheduler trigger), where it creates or updates (see the note above).
- 🔴 **The builder decides "Email or Phone is mapped" by the row's `title`**, not its `field` key (`models/actions/crm/CreateUpdateContact.ts:229-231`: `field.title === 'Email' || field.title === 'Phone'`); rows with `field: "email"` and an empty title are refused ("maps neither Email nor Phone") by the builder and by our build `[source-derived 2026-09-28; refusal observed live — live-3G-contacts-run1-title-rule.json]`. Send the drawer's titles.
- Despite the action name, this is upsert-by-email-or-phone. Without email/phone in `fields`, the validator warns and the runtime can't dedupe — producing duplicate contacts.
- `date: "currentDate"` means "set this date field to now" in an API-authored row; the validator special-cases it so `value` can be empty. The drawer never writes it for this step.
- Custom field IDs go directly in `field` (not nested under `customField`); the runtime resolves them via the contact's location schema.

cards.title: custom_code
cards.summary: Execute user-supplied JavaScript or Python and yield an `output` object that downstream steps can reference (e.g. `{{custom_code.<order>.output.<key>}}`).

fields.name: code
fields.notes: Code body in the step's `language`. It ends by assigning `output = {…}` (JS, where `return {…}` also works) or `output["k"] = …` (Python). The output is an object or an array of objects (builder note: "Output should be a JavaScript Object or Array of Objects."); its keys appear as `{{custom_code.<order>.output.<key>}}` later [source-derived 2026-09-29 — models/actions/premium-actions/CustomCode.ts:7-26; custom-code-components/CustomCodeTest.vue:58-69]. A new step is seeded with the language's sample code. 100%.

fields.name: output
fields.notes: The actual return value from a test-run. Validator requires this is non-empty — i.e. the user must test-execute before publish. 100%.

fields.name: inputData
fields.default: `{"number1": "10", "number2": "20"}` for a new builder step; `{}` when written by API without it
fields.notes: Object passed into the function as input, rebuilt from the drawer's property rows on save (max 20) [source-derived 2026-09-29 — models/actions/premium-actions/CustomCode.ts:16,53-56,108-116]. The code reads it as `inputData.<key>`: a bare `<key>` is not defined `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`. 100% (often empty).

fields.name: language
fields.notes: `"javascript"` or `"python"` (the drawer's Language picker: Javascript / Python). Switching it in the drawer resets `code`, `inputData` and `output` [source-derived 2026-09-29 — models/actions/premium-actions/CustomCode.ts:35-45; custom-code-components/hooks/listeners/use-custom-code-language-listener.ts:32-60]. 100%.

cards.validator:
`customCodeValidator` (length 297, result level `warning`). Per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json::customCodeValidator`:

```
if (!code.length)         push { field: "code",   message: "custom_code_required" }
if (isEmpty(output || {})) push { field: "output", message: "custom_code_must_be_tested" }
```

`fields_referenced: ["code", "output"]`.

The `output` check forces the user to execute the code at least once before publish — the test execution writes the function's actual return value into `output`. **You cannot publish a `custom_code` step with an empty `output`**, even if `code` is valid. To publish via API without running the UI's test step, hand-populate `output` with a sample matching what your code will actually return.
cards.notes:
- **JavaScript and Python both run, and `inputData` reaches both** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3H-code-arrays.json`: JS returned `{items, echo: inputData.k}`; Python (`language: "python"`) `output['doubled'] = int(inputData['v']) * 2` with `inputData.v = "21"` returned 42. Our build refuses a step with an empty `output` (`CODE_OUTPUT_EMPTY`, the builder's "Code must be tested before saving"); author a sample `output` — the build then runs the code through the builder's test endpoint and replaces the sample with the real result (`customCodeTests[].replacedOutput: true`).
- 🔴 **HTTP is `await customRequest.get/post/put/patch/delete/head/options(url, {data, headers, params})` returning `{data, headers, status}`; `fetch`/`require`/`axios` do not exist.** A failed request throws a **string**: `JSON.parse(e)` gives `{isAxiosError, error: <body>, status: "<code>"}`, and `e.message` is undefined. The script is killed at 60 s, and GHL's UI states a 2 MB total response limit. Inputs are `inputData.<key>` (a bare key throws `ReferenceError`); a numeric-looking input string arrives as a number, so it loses a `+`. Outputs are `{{custom_code.N.output.<key>}}`; without `.output.` the tag renders EMPTY. Also injected: `_` (lodash), `moment` (its `.tz` did not convert in a real run — see the table), `_csv.parse/stringify`, `_base64`, `_uuid`, and `fileDownloader.downloadAndUploadFormData({downloadUrl, formDataKey, uploadUrl, filename, headers})`. 🔴 `_cache` exists but every call fails (`"undefined" is not valid JSON`), even in real runs. Python (`language: "python"`) runs RestrictedPython: `requests`, `pandas`, `numpy` and `dateutil` work; `os`, `sys`, `socket` and any `_`-prefixed name are refused. See "Runtime behaviour" `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`.
- **The plugin's credential guard refuses code that writes a literal `Authorization:` label before a value** `[proven-live 2026-09-30]`. Name the header through a variable (`const AUTH = 'Authorization'; … { [AUTH]: 'Bearer ' + inputData.pit }`) and the step builds and reads back as a draft (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-W39-custom-code-example.json`). This is a limitation of OUR guard, not of GHL.
- **`output` must match the function's actual return shape.** Downstream steps reference `{{custom_code.<order>.output.<key>}}`. If you hand-fill `output: { foo: "bar" }` but your code returns `{ baz: 1 }`, the workflow publishes but downstream references break at runtime.
- **`code` is a function body** (no `function() { ... }` wrapper). JavaScript is wrapped in an **async** function, so top-level `await` works (the builder's own sample says "This is wrapped in an async function / You can use await throughout the function", and the linter wraps the code in `async() => {…}`) [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/premium-actions/CustomCode.ts:7-14; custom-code-components/hooks/use-codemirror-extensions.ts:76-81]. End with `output = {…}` or `return {…}`.
- **`inputData` keys are read as `inputData.<key>` or `inputData['<key>']`, never as bare variables.** If `inputData: { name: "{{contact.first_name}}" }`, the code reads `inputData.name` (Handlebars are resolved before the code runs); a bare `name` is not defined `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — the builder's help text; a bare-name run has not been executed]`. The builder's help text says the same: "Use inputData.keyName or inputData['keyName'] to access the values within the code" [source-derived 2026-09-26 — i18n `property_to_include_help_text`].
- **Premium gate.** `isPremiumAction: true` in the registry. When premium actions are off for the location, the drawer shows only a paywall (see Builder options and limits); whether publish is also refused on such a location is untested.
- **`stepIndex` is set** in the corpus example — premium actions often carry `stepIndex` (a numeric sequence id used internally by premium runtime infra).

Its runtime effect is under Notes. 100%.

cards.validator:
`customWebhookValidator` (length 2518, result level `warning`). Per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json::customWebhookValidator`:

1. `url` non-empty (after `.trim()`).
2. `method` set.
3. `event` set.
4. If `body.contentType === "application/json"`:
   - `body.rawData` non-empty.
   - ~~`body.rawData` is parsable JSON (`JSON.parse` in try-catch).~~ **REMOVED by GHL in the 2026-09-14
     builder bundle**, which deletes the branch and says why in its own source: *"rawData is compiled at
     execution time; merge fields make static JSON.parse invalid on save."* `[proven-live]` 2026-09-23:
     GHL's server validator (`POST …/validate-workflows`) called VALID a body containing a merge tag, a
     body of **malformed** JSON (`{"a": }`), and a body of valid JSON, identically — with a control on the
     same call path (the step's attributes stripped) refused at the action layer, so the VALIDs were real
     verdicts. So a syntax error in a JSON body is **no longer caught anywhere on GHL's save path**; it
     surfaces only when the webhook fires. The plugin's engine keeps a narrowed warning of its own
     (malformed JSON with no merge tag in it), deliberately stricter than GHL there and silent on merge tags.
5. Authorization, by type [source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/validators/webhook-validators.ts:151-210]:
   - `BEARER_TOKEN`: `authorization.data.token` set (`bearer_token_required`).
   - `API_KEY`: `authorization.data.key` and `.value` set (`api_key_and_value_required`).
   - `OAUTH2`: `authorization.data.tokenId` set (`oauth2_token_required`).
   - `BASIC_AUTH` is not checked at publish; only the drawer checks `username`/`password` (models/actions/premium-actions/CustomWebhook.ts:720-737).
6. If `saveResponse` is true: `webhookResponse.isSampleRequested` must be true and `webhookResponse.status` below 400 (`valid_sample_response_required`, field `webhookResponse`) [source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/validators/webhook-validators.ts:213-222].

`fields_referenced` (11): `authorization.data`, `authorization.data.token`, `authorization.data.tokenId`, `body.keyValueData`, `body.rawData`, `event`, `headers`, `method`, `parameters`, `url`, `webhookResponse`.
cards.notes:
- **POSTs and the receiver fires** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3J-webhook-chain.json`, `live-3J-webhook-chain-logs-late.json`: `event: CUSTOM`, `method: POST`, JSON `rawData` with a merge tag, sent to an inbound-webhook trigger URL on the same location — each run enrolled the receiving workflow once. Omit `authorization` when it is `NONE`: our tools refuse any argument KEY named `authorization` as a credential, even `{type:"NONE", data:null}`; the compiler fills that default itself.
- 🔴 **Index a response array with a DOT, never brackets.** `{{custom_webhook.N.response.<path>.numbers.0.phoneNumber}}` renders. `…numbers[0].phoneNumber` fails to compile, and the WHOLE field write is skipped (`missing-data`, "can't be compiled"), including every other tag in the same value. GHL's validator does not catch it. A whole array or object renders `[object Object]`. To pick items out of a list, pass the array into a Custom Code step, where it arrives as a real array. See "Reading an array out of the response" `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`.
- 🔴 **A 5xx holds the run on this step and retries**: 5 attempts over about 50 min, then `failed_retry_limit_reached` and the run carries on with `.status` = 500. **A 4xx fails, and the run carries on at once.** A 200 with an error in its body is a success. Branch on `{{custom_webhook.N.status}}` or `.response.<path>`. See "What a failed call does to the run" `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`.

- **`body.rawData` is a JSON-encoded string, not an object.** When you build the body programmatically, `JSON.stringify` your payload and assign the result to `rawData`. Embedded Handlebars (`{{contact.first_name}}`) remain literal strings in the JSON until the runtime resolves them at execution.
- **Nothing on GHL's save path parses `rawData` as JSON** (see the Validator section). Handlebars in the JSON must still produce valid JSON when expanded at execution. If a Handlebars value can be empty/null and you reference it without quotes (`"phone": {{contact.phone}}`), the JSON becomes invalid at runtime — wrap in quotes.
- **`webhookResponse` is a UI-test artifact.** It captures whatever the "test webhook" button produced; the runtime doesn't read it. The minimal stub `{ "isSampleRequested": false, "selectedContact": "" }` is safe **only with `saveResponse: false`**. With `saveResponse: true`, the drawer refuses Save and the publish validator warns (`valid_sample_response_required`) until a test has run (`isSampleRequested: true`) with a status below 400 [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/premium-actions/CustomWebhook.ts:808-816,942; utils/validators/webhook-validators.ts:213-222]. The test is `POST /workflow/{locationId}/run-single-action` with `{type: "custom_webhook", contactId or recordId, recordType, contactLess, locationId, attributes}` [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/premium-actions/CustomWebhook.ts:762-782; services/CustomWebhookService.ts:6-14,42-44].
- **The test follows the workflow's object** [proven-live 2026-09-29 — `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-R7-9-webhook-test-body.json`, `live-R7-9b-webhook-test-live.json`]:
  - In a company workflow the drawer asks for "SELECT A SINGLE COMPANY TO TEST", and its search is `POST /objects/business/records/search`.
  - The test sends `{contactLess: true, recordId: <company id>, recordType: "business"}`. The record type is the workflow's object key: `business` for a company workflow, `custom_objects.<key>` for a custom-object one; a contact workflow sends `contactId` instead (`getWorkflowObjectKey`, utils/workflows.ts:1635-1639).
  - One real test to an own inbound hook answered 200 "Success: test request received", and the hook recorded the request (read back separately).
  - The saved step keeps `webhookResponse: {recordId, recordType: "business", isSampleRequested: true, status: 200, data, headers}`.
  - The test is a premium action execution.
- **`saveResponse` filters the builder's merge-field menu**: only steps with `saveResponse: true` appear under "Custom Webhook" as `{{custom_webhook.<N>.response.<key>}}`. The If/Else nested dropdown lists every upstream custom webhook regardless [source-derived 2026-09-29 — utils/premium-actions-helpers/custom_webhook_helpers.ts:20-85]. The 2026-09-25 live runs all had `saveResponse: true`, so whether the tags render at runtime with `saveResponse: false` is unproven [ASSUMPTION — no builder source reads the flag at runtime; not executed].
- **`event` is a drawer preset, not a label.** `CUSTOM` (the only value seen in stored workflows) exposes Method and Content-Type. `POST` and `GET` lock the method and change the body UI (see Builder options and limits) [source-derived 2026-09-29 — models/actions/premium-actions/CustomWebhook.ts:78-91,509-531].
- **Premium gate**. `isPremiumAction: true`.
- For a simpler POST without body validation or auth, use [`webhook`](./webhook.md).

  The key is `.date`, `.datetime` or `.days` by action (`datetime_formatter_helpers.ts:11-27`)

  the log suggests `.result` — the merge tag does not.
- `.days` is numeric (`end - start`: 2026-09-01 → 2026-09-25 = `24`) `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`.
- If/Else date conditions on a formatter output use `N.<key>_system_format`
  (`datetime_formatter_helpers.ts:50,74`) `[source-derived]`.

- 🔴 **`compare_dates` on a contact DATE field miscounts.** A contact date field renders in a merge tag as `September 28, 2026`. Both dates parsed to the same day for the message, yet the count was 262 (a start of 2026-01-09 would give that). A 2020-01-01 start in the same step gave the correct 2462. Seen in two separate runs [proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3W-ifelse-output-groups.json, live-3W3-ifelse-rerun-webhook-dtf.json; the render: live-3W-ifelse-output-groups-run1-date-render.json]. - `attributes.dnd_contact` must be set, else `dnd_type_required` warning.

cards.notes:
- **All six drawer modes, proven live** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3E-dnd.json`: outbound `enable` set `dnd: true` and every channel (`Call`, `SMS`, `Email`, `WhatsApp`, `FB`, `GMB`) to `status: "active"`; `disable` set `dnd: false` and every channel `inactive`. `enable_specific` with `specific_channels: ["SMS","Email"]` touched ONLY those two (`dnd` stayed unset); `disable_specific ["SMS"]` cleared SMS and left Email active. Inbound (`dnd_direction: "inbound"`, which offers only enable/disable-all) wrote `inboundDndSettings.all` and left `dnd` / `dndSettings` untouched. Each channel row records `message: "Updated from workflow_<workflowId>"`.
- 🔴 **DND set by this step does NOT fire a `dnd_contact` trigger** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` (`live-3E-dnd-trigger17-check.json`): a published workflow whose trigger is DND (`contact.dnd == true`) evaluated all six changes and refused each with `failedReason: "DND trigger is not valid for this change"` — including the outbound enable-all that set `dnd: true`. Do not chain an opt-out workflow off a workflow-set DND.
- `dnd_direction` is in the TS interface as required, but the corpus example doesn't include it and the validator doesn't enforce it. The builder fills a missing `dnd_direction` with `'outbound'` when the drawer opens `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — components/actions/crm/SetContactDND.vue:97-99]`; what the runtime does with a stored step that lacks the key is not established.
