- `specific_channels` values are case-sensitive and mixed-case: `Call`, `SMS`, `Email`, `WhatsApp`, `FB`, `GMB` (enum `IDNDMessageTypes`) `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/ContactDND.ts:13-20]`.

cards.title: drip
cards.summary: Throttle downstream execution into batches with an inter-batch delay. The `drip` step itself is a control wrapper — downstream actions execute under the batch schedule it defines.

fields.name: interval.value
fields.notes: Wait between batches. Must be `> 0`. 100%. A new drip step is seeded with `{timeUnit: "minutes", value: 1}` and `batchSize: 100` [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/Drip.ts:18-24].

fields.name: configuredAt
fields.notes: 🔴 GHL's SERVER stamps this onto the step when the document is saved; the builder's front-end never sends it and it appears nowhere in the recovered source. Never author it. A key check that treats it as invented refuses to publish a workflow the engine itself built. `[proven-live]` 2026-09-19: sent `{batchSize, interval, type}`, read back with `configuredAt` added.

cards.notes:
- **Batch release, proven** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3D-flow.json`: `batchSize: 1`, `interval: {timeUnit: "minutes", value: 1}`, two contacts enrolled 2 s apart — the first passed at once, the second 59 s later. Limits (drawer): batch 1–10 000, interval ≤ 7 days in any unit (`models/actions/Drip.ts:15-16,72-103`).
- **Hours unit, proven** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3AP-drip-hours-days.json`, `live-3AP2-hour-readback.json`: `batchSize: 1`, `interval: {timeUnit: "hours", value: 1}`, two contacts enrolled back to back. The first passed at once. The second logged `drip_queued` at 17:43:50.6 and `drip_resume` at 18:43:49.5, one hour to the second, then ran its step. The log row types are `drip_queued` / `drip_resume`.
- **Days unit, proven** `[proven-live 2026-09-29]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3AP-drip-hours-days.json`: `interval: {timeUnit: "days", value: 1}`, two contacts. The first passed at once; the second logged `drip_queued` at 17:44:32 on day 1 and `drip_resume` at 17:44:30 on day 2 — one day of wall clock — then ran its step. The workflow was then unpublished and read back as draft.
- **`batchSize` is an integer, validated as a number.** `0` and negatives fail; `> 10000` fails.
- **All units cap at 7 days.** `value` larger than the per-unit max trips the validator. To wait longer between batches, you'd need a different mechanism (e.g. `wait` followed by `drip`).
- **Drip is a step, not a workflow-level setting.** It is registered as its own action (`type: 'drip'`, category `internal`) and throttles whatever runs after it in the path; steps before it are not throttled [source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/workflows.ts:786-795].
- **The `drip` step itself is the throttle anchor.** Downstream steps connected to its `next` execute under the batch schedule. The drip doesn't loop — it just paces the single forward path.
- **No multi-path support.** Drip is strictly linear in the corpus.
- **Cross-trigger behavior** when multiple contacts arrive while a drip is paused isn't fully traced — the docs imply contacts are queued and released in batches, but the queue mechanism isn't exposed in the workflow body.

cards.title: edit_conversation
cards.summary: "Edit Conversation": marks the enrolled contact's conversation as read or unread, and archives it or moves it back to the Recents tab.
cards.notes:
- **Strings are refused.** GHL's workflow validator refuses `read: "false"` / `archive: "true"` with `Read: Expected boolean, received string` (and the same for Archive); nothing is written [proven-live 2026-09-28 — live-3S-edit-conversation-draft-run2-ghl-strings-refused.json]. An API author must send booleans, or let the plugin compile the drawer strings (it mirrors the asset's transform).
- **`read`**: `false` sets the conversation's `unreadCount` to 1, `true` sets it to 0 [proven-live 2026-09-28 — live-3S-edit-conversation.json].
- **`archive`**: `true` sets `inbox: false` and the conversation leaves the `recents` search; `false` sets `inbox: true` and it returns [proven-live 2026-09-28 — live-3S2-edit-conversation-archive.json]. On a conversation that had never been in the inbox (`inbox` absent, created by API with no message), `archive: true` left `inbox` absent [proven-live 2026-09-28 — live-3S-edit-conversation.json].
- **The run log's `data.conversation` is not the resulting state.** In one run it reported `unreadCount: 1` while the read-back on a separate request showed 0. Read the conversation back instead [proven-live 2026-09-28 — live-3S2-edit-conversation-archive.json].
- **It needs a conversation.** Every run in the proof acted on an existing conversation; a contact with none was not tested.

cards.validator:
`sendEmailActionValidator` (length 582, result level `warning`). Per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json::sendEmailActionValidator`:

- Walks the conditional above.
- For `template_id` set, returns a `resource: "email_template"` lookup that the publish endpoint resolves against the template store. If the template doesn't exist, publish rejects.

Field index per `sniffs/bundle/validators-summary.json::sendEmailActionValidator`: `["html", "subject", "template_id"]`.
cards.notes:
- 🔴 **"Send to associated contacts"** — `emailRecipients` (`enrolled_contacts` | `most_recently_associated` | `earliest_associated` | `all_associated_contacts`) with `associationLabels[{associationId, label?}]` (`Email.ts:108-164`). Our tools store both as authored; on a location without the `workflows.associationEmail` lab the email drawer shows NO associated-contacts control, so a person cannot see or change the stored mode `[proven-live 2026-09-29 — `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/W22-LIVE-PROOFS.md` rows 6, 6b]`. In Company workflows the builder locks the mode to `all_associated_contacts` `[source-derived — Email.ts:1272-1280]`.
- **cc / bcc and template mode, proven live** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3BA-email-cc-template.json`: one send with `cc` and `bcc` (comma-separated strings on the step) arrived on the message record as `cc: [<addr>]`, `bcc: [<addr>]` beside `to`. The same step used a saved email-builder template (`template_id` + `templatesource: "email-builder"`, no `html` on the step), and the sent body was the template's HTML.
- **From set from custom values, on a domain the location cannot send from** `[proven-live 2026-09-29]`: with
  `from_name: "{{custom_values.<name>}}"` and `from_email: "{{custom_values.<email>}}"` holding an `@example.org`
  address, the delivered record read `from: "<the custom value's name> <local+example.org@<sending subdomain>>"`. The
  NAME rendered as authored. The ADDRESS kept its local part and domain as a plus-tag, rewritten onto the sending
  subdomain the message record names (`meta.email.channel: "leadconnector"`). It did not fall back to the location's
  default sender. The step's execution log shows the unrewritten `tcwf-…@example.org`, so read the conversation message
  (`GET /conversations/messages/email/{id}` → `from`), not the log, to see what was sent. A client-account report said
  both name and address fell back to the location default; that was not reproduced here. That account's own sending-domain
  setup may differ `[inferred — from the rewrite target being the location's sending subdomain]`
  (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-W25-fromclick-readback.json`).
- **Click tracking wraps literal and custom-value links, NOT a contact-field link** `[proven-live 2026-09-29, same send]`:
  with `trackingOptions.hasTrackingLinks: true`, `<a href="https://…">`, `<a href="{{custom_values.<url>}}">` and
  `<a href="{{contact.website}}">` went out as two `…/email-tracking/<id>?contactId=…` redirects (on the agency's
  white-label host) and the contact's raw website URL. A link whose href is a contact merge tag is not tracked, so
  "clicked a specific link" conditions cannot see it.
- **LEAD — a custom-value link's tracked redirect may be frozen at first creation** `[lead 2026-09-30: an observation on a client account by another session, read-only; unproven on the test sub-account]`: the tracked link (`…/email-tracking/<id>`) for `<a href="{{custom_values.<url>}}">` was minted once and reused. After the custom value was changed, later sends carried the SAME tracking id and it still redirected to the OLD value (three emails, two workflows, read by GET without following redirects). A link built from a contact merge field is sent unwrapped and resolves per contact at send time (each contact's email carried that contact's own field value). Setting `trackingOptions.hasTrackingLinks: false` on the step removes the wrapper: re-sent emails then carry the current custom value directly. The wrapper id belongs to the email LINK, not to a contact or a send (the same id on sends to two contacts an hour apart); a step whose href was changed from a contact-field link to a custom-value link got a fresh wrapper id at its first send. Not measured: whether re-saving an unchanged body keeps the old wrapper. If it holds, a custom-value href is frozen once sent, and link tracking off is the workaround. To prove it here: a throwaway email with a custom-value href sent to an own contact, the custom value changed, the body re-saved unchanged, sent again, ids and redirects compared.
- **Attachment and tracking off, proven live** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3AV-email-cc-attach-internal.json`: `attachments: [{name, url, size}]` pointing at a file in the location's media library was stored as written, and the sent message is flagged `hasAttachments: true`. With `trackingOptions` all `false`, the body link went out as the original URL, not rewritten to a tracking link (with tracking on it is rewritten, see [mailgun_email_event](../triggers/mailgun_email_event.md)).
- **Sends, proven live** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3I-sends.json`: inline `subject` + `html` to a contact with an email logged `success`, "Email queued successfully.", and created an outbound conversation message whose meta carries the `workflowId` / `workflowStepId`; `{{contact.first_name}}` in the subject rendered.
- **Email "add tag when" rules live on the server, not only in `attributes.conditions`.** The drawer reads them from `GET {marketplaceBackend}/emails/trigger/campaign/{locationId}/{workflowId}:{actionId}` and writes them with `POST` to the same path (`{ triggers: [...] }`); one is removed with `DELETE {marketplaceBackend}/emails/trigger/{locationId}/{triggerId}`. On open it replaces `attributes.conditions` with the server list (empty server list → `[]`). The builder treats the server list as the truth; whether a `conditions` array written into the step by API alone creates any rule is not established `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — services/EmailService.ts:139-195; components/actions/SendEmailRevamp.vue:994-1030; AdditionalSettings.vue:337-360]`.

- 🔴 **`template_id: "none"` is a sentinel the BUILDER understands — do not send it over the API.**
  In the builder it is a switch: `selectTemplate` clears `template_id` and `templatesource` and the
  email goes inline `[source-derived]`. On the wire it is NOT equivalent to omitting the key:
  `POST /workflow/{loc}/validate-assets` faults `template_id: "none"` with
  *"Referenced Email Template does not exist or does not belong to this location"* — the SAME finding
  a bogus id gets — while omitting the key, or sending `""`, is clean
  `[proven-live, 2026-09-12, sniffs/live-2026-09-12-peer-batch2]`. So an inline email omits
  `template_id`; the engine drops a literal `"none"` before the wire for exactly this reason.
  Don't confuse either with a missing template causing a publish error.
- **`html` is auto-cleaned** via `cleanHTMLForEmail` before validation; whitespace-only HTML fails validation.
- **`htmlDefaults`** is injected back into the `html` as `data-cv-defaults` attributes (per `Email.ts::save`). The map on its own does nothing at send; the inline attribute is what the send reads `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`. See the defaults section above.
- **`from_name` without `from_email` is invalid**. The UI prevents save, but a hand-written payload can carry only `from_name` — publish will reject via the model's `validateFrom` getter.
- **`templatesource === "email-builder"` triggers a side fetch** of the template details during save (`templateService.getWorkflowTemplate`); a stale `template_id` here will set `isCloned: true` unless `syncEnabled` is set. Behavior on the API side without the UI's pre-flight isn't fully traced — sending a stale `template_id` is likely accepted by publish.
- For sending email inside an `internal_notification` envelope, this same `IEmail` shape is nested under `attributes.email`. See [`internal_notification`](./internal_notification.md).
- The validator emits warnings, not errors, but publish treats both as blocking.

cards.validator:
`eventStartDateValidator` (per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json`):

- `event_start_type` must be set, else `event_start_type_required`.
- `value` must not be empty/undefined, else `event_start_value_required`.
- If `event_start_type === "custom_field"` and `value` is set, `value` must be a valid handlebar (`isValidHandleBar(value)`), else `event_start_invalid_custom_variable`.

Per `validators-summary.json`: 2 fields referenced (`event_start_type`, `value`); result level `warning`.
cards.notes:
- **`recurring` in the builder's value shape, proven live** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3AR-goal-opp-esd-atw.json`: `recurring_type: "day_week"`, `value: 1` (Monday, run on a Monday) and `recurring_type: "day_month"`, `value: 28` (run on the 28th), each with `recurring_time: "19:15"` (account zone, a quarter hour ≈ 17 min ahead). A following `appointment` wait 3 minutes BEFORE released both at exactly 19:12. So the anchor is TODAY at that time when today is the named day. What happens when the time has already passed today is not measured. (An earlier specimen stored `value: "monday"` and `recurring_time: "9:00 AM"`; the engine accepted them, but the builder never writes that shape, and it was never run.)

- **The anchor feeds the `appointment` wait** (there is no `event_date` wait type — `WaitType`, `models/conditions/Wait.ts:116-129`) `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3L-event-start.json`: with `event_start_type: "datetime"` set to T (ISO with the account timezone offset), a following wait `type: "appointment"`, `appointmentStartAfter: {when: "before", type: "minutes", value: 3}` released ≈ T−3 (≈ 30 s late) and `when: "after", value: 1` released at T+1 to the second. With `event_start_type: "custom_field"` and `{{contact.<date field>}}` holding a past date, the wait logged "Event Start Date wait time was in the past (…). Moving to the next step." (`appointmentCondition: "next"`). No appointment exists anywhere in these runs.
- `event_start_type` has exactly three values: `"datetime"`, `"custom_field"`, `"recurring"` `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/EventStartDate.ts:6]`.

cards.summary: Look up a contact by one or more field values; branch into "Contact found" / "Contact not found" paths.

A legacy step without `convertToMultipath` saves none and runs linear. `[source-derived — FindContact.ts:254-296]`

cards.validator:
`findContactValidator` (per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json`):

- `attributes.fields.length > 0` else `at_least_one_field_required`.
- For each row: `field` must be set; `value` must be set unless `date === "currentDate"` or value is `false`/`0`.
- Non-standard `field` values trigger `custom_field` resource warning.

Note: `find_contact` does **not** require email/phone (unlike `create_update_contact`). The drawer offers 13 standard fields (Contact ID included; not Date of birth, DND, Country, Timezone or Contact type) and only text-like custom fields (see Builder options and limits).
cards.notes:
- **In a contact-less run it really searches, and Found ATTACHES the contact** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `live-3J2-find-contactless.json`: first step of an inbound-webhook run — an email that exists took Found and the run's enrolment became that contact's; an email that exists nowhere took Not Found (a `create_update_contact` there created the contact). After Found, a `create_update_contact` in that branch was skipped (the run already holds a contact), so it changed nothing.
- **Custom-field and phone searches, contact-less** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3AS-find-contactless-cf-phone.json`: first step of an inbound-webhook run.
  - A row on a custom text field (`field: "<customFieldId>"`) holding a key that one contact has took Found. The run's enrolment became that contact, and a tag step in the Found branch tagged it. A key that exists nowhere ran with no contact (Not Found) and created nothing.
  - A `phone` row given the contact's number in E.164 (`+1555…`) found it.
  - 🔴 The same number in US national format (`(555) 555-0177`) found **nothing**. The account's country is GB, so a national-format number is presumably read against the account's country [inferred from the account country; not tested on a US account]. Send phone searches in E.164.
- 🔴 **Skipped in any run that already has a contact** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3G-contacts.json`: enrolled with a contact, the step logs `skipped`, `skippedFor: {type: "missing-data", msg: "Only one contact is allowed per workflow, and <contact name> is already in use."}` and does nothing. It is for runs that start WITHOUT a contact (e.g. an inbound-webhook or scheduler trigger), where it really searches (see the note above, `live-3J2-find-contactless.json`). 🔴 **A skipped find routes down the FOUND branch**: all three runs (an existing email, an address that exists nowhere, a custom-field value) took Contact Found. A find on a contact workflow therefore always "finds".
- Hybrid action: `next` is a string array (transition IDs), not a single string. See `docs/04-workflow-anatomy.md §4` for multi-path semantics.
- The two `transitions` entries are **created by the builder on save** (when fewer than two exist and branching is enabled), not when the step is dropped — server may reject the step body if transitions are missing or condition values are mistyped.
- A primary branch (`isPrimaryBranch: true`) is the visual "happy path" — the workflow engine doesn't treat it preferentially at runtime; both branches are evaluated by their `condition`.
- Sibling action `find_or_create_contact` (not in this registry but in metadata) covers the "create-if-not-found" combo as a single step.

cards.notes:
- **`__customInputFields__[].value` is the operator, not the value.** The operand is in `secondValue`. This is the inverse of intuition — verify before constructing filter rows by hand.
- **The two transitions are hard-required** for the runtime even though no validator enforces them. Sending `transitions: []` will publish but produce a step with no branches at runtime.

There is no `"oldest"`.

Each run found the contact's card on that pipeline and marked it won. **What `sorting` picks is NOT measured.** The earliest-vs-latest differential needs two open cards for one contact in one pipeline, and the test location refuses the second (`OPPORTUNITY_NO_DUPLICATE`, because duplicate opportunities are disabled in its CRM settings). Only one card existed per run, so both sort orders found that same card.
- **Empty filter (`__customInputFields__: []`)** is observed; what the runtime matches in that case isn't traced (presumably "any opportunity on the contact").
- **`workflowsActionType: "INTERNAL"`** sibling marker — internal helper, not in user picker.
- For non-multi-path opportunity lookups inside `if_else` conditions, see `if_else`'s `conditionType` enums.

cards.title: goto
cards.summary: Jump execution to another step in the **same workflow**. Used to close loops or merge branches back together.

meta.Hybrid / multi-path?: Linear (must be at end of its branch)

fields.name: targetNodeId
fields.notes: **In-workflow step UUID** to jump to. References a sibling node by `id` within the same workflow's `workflowData.templates[]`. 100%.

fields.name: loopIdentified
fields.notes: UI hint that the goto closes a detected loop. Optional, builder-set.

cards.validator:
`gotoValidator` (length 352, result level `warning`). Per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json::gotoValidator`:

```
1. If parentNode.next is truthy → push { field: "placement", message: "goto_must_be_at_end_of_branch" }
2. If targetNodeId is set AND templates does not contain a row with id === targetNodeId
   → push { field: "targetNodeId", message: "target_node_not_found" }
```

Two distinct enforcements:

| Check | Field | Message key |
|---|---|---|
| Goto must be last step in its branch | `placement` | `goto_must_be_at_end_of_branch` |
| Target must exist in current workflow | `targetNodeId` | `target_node_not_found` |

`fields_referenced: ["placement", "targetNodeId"]` per `validators-summary.json`.
cards.notes:
- **Jumps forward and must end its branch** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3D-flow.json`: a goto as the last step of an If/Else Yes branch, targeting the SECOND step of the Else branch, ran that step and skipped the first (`tcwf-3d-b-skipped` never added). A goto in the middle of a branch is refused by our compiler (`GOTO_NOT_TERMINAL`), matching the builder, which ends a branch at a goto.
- 🔴 **Deleting a goto's edge on the advanced canvas leaves a goto the canvas cannot re-target.** The edge IS `targetNodeId`: deleting it and saving removes the attribute and GHL's validator refuses the workflow. After a reload, drawing a new edge from that goto marks the workflow unsaved but Save stays disabled (the builder's save gate refuses while any goto lacks a target and only the standard builder clears it `[source-derived]` `states/workflow.ts:1152-1167,1493-1509`). Repair: write `targetNodeId` through the API and read it back `[proven-live 2026-09-29]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/ui/UI-WALK-CANVAS-3CM.md` (gestures 31-32). A goto has no ⏸ button; ⇧D disables it and ⇧E re-enables it.
- **`targetNodeId` is an in-workflow reference.** It must be the `id` of another node in the same workflow's `workflowData.templates[]`. **Not** a trigger id, not a workflow id. The validator verifies existence against the current body's templates only — cross-workflow gotos are impossible.
- **Goto must be a terminal step in its branch.** If a goto has `next: "<some-uuid>"`, the placement validator fails. To put a goto mid-flow, remove the `next` pointer from it (the goto itself becomes the leaf).
- **The validator's `targetNodeId` check is local to the request payload.** If you publish a workflow containing a goto pointing to a node that exists in a separate auto-saved draft but not in the published body, publish will reject.
- **`loopIdentified: true` is metadata for the UI's loop-detection routine** — it doesn't change runtime behavior.
- **No cycle prevention.** Two gotos can point at each other (A → B's goto, B → A's goto), producing an infinite loop. The runtime has its own loop-execution cap (not extracted here); publish accepts the graph.
- For jumping into a **different** workflow, use [`add_to_workflow`](./add_to_workflow.md) instead.

cards.validator: No publish validator runs against `if_else`. The registry entry has no `validation.code` (per `sniffs/bundle/registry-parsed.json::entries[]::if_else`), and `validators.json` contains no `ifElseValidator`. Empty / malformed branches will not block publish — they just produce a node that never routes anyone.
cards.notes:
- **AND / OR, and branch order, proven live** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`:
  - A segment's `operator: "or"` matches when ANY of its conditions holds. A branch "tag X OR tag Y" took contacts holding only X, and only Y, and sent a contact with neither to Else. The same two conditions with `operator: "and"` sent the X-only contact to Else (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3AW-ifelse-or-wave11.json`). The builder toggles this operator per segment (`components/conditions/Segments.vue:69-83`), and `branch.operator` joins several segments the same way [source-derived].
  - A contact matching only the second of two conditioned branches took the second (`live-3AA-ifelse-invoice-payment.json`), and two AND-ed tag conditions let only the contact holding both through (`live-3AQ-delete-contact.json`). Which branch wins when SEVERAL match is not measured.

- **`contact_reply` conditions, measured on live replies** `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`:
  - `matches_intent == schedule-yes` is an AI classification. The row logs `waiting`, then the result. "Yes approve it" gave true, **"looks good" gave true**, and "1" gave false.
  - `message.body contain "yes"` is **case-insensitive**: it matched "Yes approve it".
  - `message.body == "1"` matched only "1" `sniffs/afy-onboarding-tests-2026-09-25/live-O-batch.json`.
- **An `opportunities` condition on a custom field** (`conditionSubType: <fieldId>`) reads the run's ASSOCIATED card. With none, it falls to the else branch even when the contact's card holds the value `[proven-live 2026-09-25]` `sniffs/afy-onboarding-tests-2026-09-25/live-O-batch.json`.
- **Both `parent` and `parentKey` are required** on branch children. Some corpus rows duplicate the parent id in both fields. See [`docs/06-fields-glossary.md §1`](../../10-anatomy/06-fields-glossary.md).
- **No publish validator** means an `if_else` parent with `branches: []` passes publish but does nothing. Don't rely on publish to catch broken branching.
- The `if_else` parent node has `nodeType: "condition-node"`. Each branch is a separate step (also `type: "if_else"`) with `nodeType: "branch-yes"` — legacy binary form also uses `branch-no` for the else fallthrough. Branch entries are children of the parent via `parent` / `parentKey`; peer branches reference each other through `sibling[]`. Per [`docs/04-workflow-anatomy.md §4.2`](../../10-anatomy/04-workflow-anatomy.md) and `sniffs/FIELDS_GLOSSARY.json::nodeType` (only three observed values: `condition-node`, `branch-yes`, `branch-no` — `"branch"` is not one of them).
- `currentRecipeType: "CUSTOM"` is the catch-all when the UI's recipe picker isn't used; recipe-scaffolded `if_else`s carry a non-CUSTOM value.
- `segments` (top-level on attributes) is legacy; new bodies use `branches[].segments`.
- **At most 10 branches.** The drawer blocks Add branch once `attributes.branches` has 10 entries. Each branch has a menu with **Duplicate branch** (and Delete when more than one branch remains), and branches can be **dragged to reorder**, which reorders the `attributes.branches` array (the drag handle is hidden when the same editor is used inside a condition wait) [source-derived 2026-09-26 — components/conditions/new/Branch.vue:4-7,172-174,183-197,260-288]. Whether the runtime evaluates branches in array order is not proven here.
- For the cross-cutting multi-path mechanics, see [`docs/04-workflow-anatomy.md §4`](../../10-anatomy/04-workflow-anatomy.md).

- 🔴 **Not buildable on the sandbox, runtime UNPROVEN — needs a connected Instagram account on the sandbox; third-party integrations are out of scope (coordinator 2026-09-28).** `[blocked 2026-09-28]` GHL refuses to store the step at all without it (its asset check names the missing connection / sub-account) (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3O-blocked-drafts.json`).

After the call action, the contact will move to the 'Default Timeout' branch." `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/InteractiveMessenger.ts:132-149]`.

cards.validator:
`internalNotificationValidator` (length 1433, result level `warning`). Per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json::internalNotificationValidator`:

1. If `type` is missing → push `{ field: "type", message: "notification_type_required" }`. Return.
2. Switch on `type`:
   - `"email"`: require `attributes.email`; if `email.template_id` is unset, require `email.subject.trim()` and `email.html.trim()`.
   - `"sms"`: require `attributes.sms`; unless `sms.template_id` is set, require `sms.body.trim()`.
   - `"whatsapp"`: require `attributes.whatsapp`; unless `whatsapp.template_id` is set, require `whatsapp.body.trim()`.
   - `"notification"`: require `attributes.notification.body.trim()` (the warning's `field` label is `notification.message`).

`[source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/validators/communication-validators.ts:123-230]`

Per `sniffs/bundle/validators-summary.json::internalNotificationValidator`, `fields_referenced` has 10 entries:

```
email, email.html, email.subject,
notification, notification.message,
sms, sms.body,
type,
whatsapp, whatsapp.body
```

The required field set thus depends entirely on `type` — only one channel sub-object is enforced per save.
cards.notes:
- **Email, SMS and WhatsApp notifications carry the same recipient controls as in-app**: `userType: "assign"` with `assignedOwners`, the "Notify followers" toggles `alsoNotifyContactFollowers` / `alsoNotifyOpportunityFollowers`, and on email a `bcc`. Stored as authored and rendered by the drawer (owners, Contact followers ON, Bcc shown) `[proven-live 2026-09-29 — `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/W22-LIVE-PROOFS.md` row 6]`. WhatsApp offers only `assign` or `user` (`WhatsApp.ts getUserTypeOptions`); an assign notification with no `assignedOwners` means contact owner (the builder's backward-compatible default).
- **Channels and recipients, proven live** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3I-sends.json`: in-app (`type: "notification"`) to a selected user and to the contact's assigned owner (`userType: "assign"`, after an assign step) — both `accepted`; email to a selected user — `accepted`; SMS and WhatsApp to a user with no phone — `skipped`, "No phone number found for user." Email to a **custom address** (`email.userType: "custom_email"` + `email.to`), run on a contact with no email, was stored as written and the step logged `accepted` with a request id `[proven-live 2026-09-28 — live-3AV-email-cc-attach-internal.json]`. Delivery itself is not readable through the API.
- 🔴 **`userType: "all"` notifies EVERY user on the account.** Our compiler defaults `userType` to `all` when neither `userType` nor `selectedUser` is authored — always author the recipient.
- **`type` is the channel discriminator** — only the matching sub-object is validated. You may include other sub-objects (e.g. carry both `email` and `sms` in the body) but only one runs at execution.
- **The in-app message text is `notification.body`.** The validator checks `attributes.notification.body?.trim()`; `notification.message` is only the `field` label on its warning. There is no `message` key to write `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/validators/communication-validators.ts:213-228; models/actions/Notification.ts:14-25]`.
- **Channel sub-objects reuse other actions' interfaces**. `email` is `IEmail`, `sms` is `ISMS`. The same `template_id: "none"` switch from [`email`](./email.md) applies inside `internal_notification`. Likewise `attachments` formatting.
- **`userType` lives on the channel sub-object**, not on the top-level `attributes` — even though `IInternalNotification.userType` is declared at the top, the corpus and the validator both look inside the sub-object.
- 🔴 **GHL does not check a Custom Number's `to`.** The builder's own check (`isToFieldValid`, `SMS.ts`) refuses `custom_sms` with no `to`, but GHL's server validator answered `valid: true` on a step with `userType: "custom_sms"` and no `to` `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`. A step written by API without the number saves, validates and publishes, and it has no recipient. This project's workflow engine refuses `custom_sms` without `to`, as it already refused `custom_email` without `to`.
- **WhatsApp channel rarely used** (2 corpus rows). Treat its publish behavior as untested in production payloads built outside the UI.

cards.title: internal_update_opportunity
cards.summary: Internal helper that updates an existing opportunity. Used by AI-driven and migration paths — different attribute shape from the user-facing [`create_opportunity`](./create_opportunity.md).

meta.Section: Not registered in `registry-parsed.json` (internal helper, not picker-visible)
meta.Premium / beta?: No (but flagged `workflowsActionType: "INTERNAL"` on the step row)

fields.name: __customInputFields__
fields.notes: The actual update spec. Each entry: `{ __customInputs__, value, filterField, valueFieldType, dataType? }`. 100%.

fields.name: __customInputs__
fields.notes: Top-level scratch space; always empty in corpus. 100%.

fields.name: allowBackward
fields.notes: Allow moving to an earlier stage. 100%.

cards.validator: **None in the bundle.** `validator: null`, `validator_delegation_chain: []`, `required_fields_per_validator: []` per `og-action-ui-metadata.json::internal_update_opportunity`; no `internalUpdateOpportunityValidator` in `validators.json` — this is an INTERNAL marketplace asset. Required-ness comes from the asset's `inputs[].required` (and its dynamic-field generator). The asset carries its own `validation` function: a negative `monetaryValue` in `__customInputFields__` fails with "Opportunity value should be a numeric value" `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — sniffs/workflows-domain-recon-2026-09-25/marketplace-assets-2026-09-25.json internal_update_opportunity.validation]`. Whether publish runs that function on an API-built step is not established; the runtime may be stricter.
cards.notes:
- 🔴 **Unbound update → a `skipped` row, not silence** `[proven-live 2026-09-26]`: `{success:false, isSkipped:true, msg: "Internal Action Error - Please use Opportunity trigger/find opportunity action to get the opportunity"}`; the card is untouched and the run continues. Reproduced three ways: in a workflow WITH an opportunity trigger entered by direct enrolment (a contact without a card, and one holding an open card — `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-C3-opp-condition.json`), and in a trigger-less workflow under `find_opportunity`'s Not-Found branch (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-C4-opp-control.json`). 
- **What binds a card for this step** `[proven-live 2026-09-26]`: an opportunity trigger, a `find_opportunity` Found branch, or an earlier `internal_create_opportunity` on the path. After `find_opportunity` (pipeline filter, `latest`) the step wrote the found card only (a Won card in another pipeline was untouched) `sniffs/afy-onboarding-tests-2026-09-25/live-O-batch.json`; after `internal_create_opportunity` it wrote the card that step made (`won`). A native [`create_opportunity`](./create_opportunity.md) does NOT bind: the same update after it logged the `skipped` row above and the card stayed `open` (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-W24-create-binds.json`). A 2026-09-25 run (`live-O-batch.json`) read NO log row for an unbound update; every later unbound run (`live-C-opportunity.json`, `live-C3-opp-condition.json`, `live-C4-opp-control.json`, `live-W24-create-binds.json`) wrote the `skipped` row, so read the logs a while after the run before concluding the step did not run.
- A date custom field accepts `{{right_now.date}}`. It stored `2026-09-25` (YYYY-MM-DD) `[proven-live 2026-09-25]` `sniffs/afy-onboarding-tests-2026-09-25/live-O-batch.json`.
- **`workflowsActionType: "INTERNAL"`** is the top-level marker (sibling of `attributes`) that distinguishes internal-helper rows from user-authored ones. The UI hides these unless an internal path created them.
- **The `__customInputFields__` shape mirrors a custom-object filter UI** — same `filterField` / `value` / `valueFieldType` keys as filter rows elsewhere. The "update" is encoded as a list of field-write directives.
- **No validator means no publish-time existence check** on pipeline/stage ids. Verify your `value`s out-of-band.
- **Most corpus rows update `status` or `pipelineStageId`.** Some carry two entries (pipeline + stage) to relocate the opp.
- **The lack of `opportunityId` field** suggests the runtime targets the contact's "current" opportunity (the one matched by an upstream `find_opportunity` step). Not verified — but the pattern is consistent in corpus workflows that pair `find_opportunity` → `internal_update_opportunity`.

cards.title: loop
cards.summary: A container step that runs the steps inside its body once per item of a list, one item after another.

fields.name: name
fields.notes: drawer "Action name"; the step's own `name`, not an attribute

cards.notes:
- 🔴 **`items` must be one expression.** The backend's structural validator (`loop-items-single-expression`) accepts exactly
  one `{{ … }}`; anything concatenated compiles to a string, which **iterates zero times** [source-derived — Loop.ts:5-9].
- **Not allowed inside a body:** `loop` (no nesting in V1), `workflow_goal`, `goto`, `remove_from_workflow`,
  `remove_from_all_workflows` (they end the execution, so the loop's barrier stalls until a watchdog releases it), and
  event/condition waits (`appointment`, `service_booking`, `rental_booking`, `overdue`, `reply`, `user_replied`,
  `link_clicked`, `email_event`, `condition`); time waits are allowed [source-derived — loop.helper.ts:95-140].
- **A loop with no body is refused** (`checkLoopHasBody`).
- **The plugin does not author a loop.** Its engine refuses one by name (`LOOP_NOT_AUTHORED`) before anything is written;
  before 2026-09-29 it compiled an authored loop as a straight line [proven-live 2026-09-29 — refusal returned, nothing
  written: `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/W23-LIVE-PROOFS.md` row 3]. Add the loop in the builder where it is offered; an
  edit leaves an existing loop and its body as stored.
- On the advanced canvas the body is drawn as a container box around the tagged steps.

cards.validator:
`mathOperationValidator` (per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json`):

- `selectField` must be set, else `math_select_field_required`.
- If `selectField` matches `{{math_operation.\d+.result}}`, the validator walks `templates` to ensure the referenced math step still exists; warns `math_source_action_deleted` otherwise, or `math_input_field_type_changed` if the source's type changed.
- When `updateField` is set and doesn't reference `custom_values`, the source and target types must match for `numerical` / `date`, else `math_field_type_mismatch`.
- The only operator check is divide-by-zero: a `div` row whose value is the number `0` warns `math_division_by_zero` (a merge tag resolving to 0 is not caught) `[source-derived — utils/validators/additional-action-validators.ts:392-399]`.

Per `validators-summary.json`: 3 fields referenced (operators, selectField, updateField); result level `warning`.
cards.notes:
- **Output** `{{math_operation.N.result}}` (per-type `stepIndex`) is readable by later steps, with or without `updateField` `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`. A custom VALUE as source and target runs too `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3M-custom-value.json`): `selectField`/`updateField` = `{{custom_values.<key>}}` with `sourceCustomValueId`/`targetCustomValueId` = its id, `add 2` on `5` → the custom value read `7` and `.result` rendered `7`.
- **A MONETORY custom field is a numerical source** (`MATH_FIELD_TYPES`, `MathOperations.ts:20`): in place (`selectField` = `updateField`) `100.5 + 0.25` → `100.75` `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`. Custom fields are addressed by field ID in `selectField` / `updateField` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3B-fields-math.json`.
- **Date source** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`: `2026-01-31` with `add {days:1, months:1, years:1}` → `2027-03-01`; the result merge tag renders `YYYY-MM-DD` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3B-fields-math.json`.
- 🔴 **Operators run left to right and the result is ROUNDED to 2 decimals** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`: source 10, operators `add 5, mul 2, sub 1, div 3` in ONE step → `9.67` (((10+5)×2−1)÷3 = 9.666…). A second step reading `{{math_operation.1.result}}` × 10 → `96.7` — it inherits the rounded value `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3B-fields-math.json`.
- `selectField` and `updateField` are the **same value** in the corpus example — this is the in-place increment pattern.
- Chaining: a downstream math step can reference `{{math_operation.N.result}}` where N is the step index. The validator tracks template changes that would invalidate the reference.
- `math_operation` and `number_formatter` are two different current step types; an older README conflated them. Arithmetic is `math_operation`; formatting/parsing/random is [`number_formatter`](./number_formatter.md).

meta.Premium / beta?: Not listed as premium by the engine's readiness check

fields.name: format.fromFieldType
fields.notes: MUST equal the part before `_to_` in `action`, else the step is SKIPPED at run time `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`.

cards.validator:
`numberFormatterValidator` — warnings only. Per action: `string_to_number` → `format.fromField`,
`inputDecimalMark`; `string_to_formatted_number` → + `outputNumberFormat`; `number_to_phone` →
`fromField`, `phone.format`; `number_to_currency` → `fromField`, `currency.currencyCode/currencyLocale`;
`random_number` → `random.min/max/decimalPlaces`. It does NOT check `fromFieldType`.
cards.notes:
- **`fromFieldType` / `toFieldType` must match the action name.** The builder derives them by
  splitting the action on `_to_` (`number_to_currency` → `number` / `currency`;
  `NumberFormatter.ts:356-361`). Author `fromFieldType: "string"` on `number_to_currency` and the
  step saves, passes GHL's validator and our build, then is **skipped at run time**:
  `status: skipped`, `skippedFor: {type: "invalid-data", msg: "Source field type must be number.
  Given -> fromFieldType: string"}` — and its output renders empty `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`.
- The output is `{{number_formatter.N.result}}` (`number_formatter_helpers.ts:51`); `N` is the
  per-type 1-based `stepIndex`. `number_to_currency` on `1234.5` rendered `$1,234.50`
  `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`.

```
if (!removeAll && (!tags || tags.length === 0) && !customTags)
  push { field: "tags", message: "at_least_one_tag_required" }
```

Three publishable shapes:

| Shape | Required |
|---|---|
| Remove specific tags | `tags: [...]` non-empty |
| Remove via custom-text mode | `customTags` non-empty |
| Remove all tags | `removeAll: true` |

`fields_referenced: ["tags"]`.
cards.notes:
- **Three modes proven live** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3A-crm-basics.json`: `tags:[x]` removed only `x`; Dynamic `customTags` with a merge tag removed the resolved tag; `removeAll: true` removed EVERY tag on the contact — including tags other systems rely on — and the run continued to the next step.
- **`removeAll: true` is the nuclear option** — strips every tag from the contact. The runtime doesn't allow scoped "all tags matching prefix X"; for that, you'd need explicit `tags: [...]` enumeration.
- **`tags` match is case-insensitive** (matches tag storage convention). `["sba"]` removes both `"sba"` and `"SBA"` if both exist.
- **Tags that don't exist on the contact are silently ignored.** No error, no branch.
- **`customTags` is the "Dynamic" (custom-value / merge-tag) input mode** — one text value; the builder keeps only one of `tags` / `customTags` on save `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/ContactTag.ts:50-55]`. Rarely seen in corpus.

cards.summary: Drop the running contact from one or more other workflows (or all of them).

fields.name: workflow_id
fields.notes: Target workflow UUID(s). Polymorphic: corpus shows both single string and array forms. 98.0%.

fields.name: allWorkflows
fields.notes: `true` for the two "all workflows" modes (skips the `workflow_id` check). Absent for "current" and "another". On load the builder forces `allWorkflows = true` whenever the `includeCurrent` key is present `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/RemoveFromWorkflow.ts:29-31,68-81]`. 2.0%.

fields.name: includeCurrent
fields.notes: With `allWorkflows: true`: `false` = every workflow except this one, `true` = every workflow including this one. Absent for "current" and "another" `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/RemoveFromWorkflow.ts:68-81]`. 2.0%.

cards.validator:
`removeFromWorkflowValidator` (length 307, result level `warning`). Per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json::removeFromWorkflowValidator`:

```
if (!allWorkflows) {
  if ("includeCurrent" in attributes) return []   // early-return — skips workflow_id check
  if (!workflow_id || (Array.isArray && workflow_id.length === 0))
    push { field: "workflow_id", message: "workflow_selection_required" }
}
return []
```

The builder offers four modes (`updateTypeSelection`); each writes one stored shape `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/RemoveFromWorkflow.ts:68-109; components/actions/crm/AddToWorkflow.vue:238-282]`:

| UI mode | Stored shape |
|---|---|
| `current` — Current workflow | `workflow_id: ["<this workflow's id>"]`, no `allWorkflows` / `includeCurrent` |
| `another` — Another workflow | `workflow_id: ["<id>", …]` (non-empty array), no `allWorkflows` / `includeCurrent` |
| `all_except_current` — All workflows except current | `allWorkflows: true, includeCurrent: false`, no `workflow_id` |
| `all` — All workflows | `allWorkflows: true, includeCurrent: true`, no `workflow_id` |

In AI-tool mode (`useAsTool`) only `another` and `all_except_current` are offered `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/RemoveFromWorkflow.ts:103-106]`. On reopen the drawer derives the mode from the shape: a single `workflow_id` equal to the current workflow reads as `current`; no `workflow_id` at all is filled with the current workflow and reads as `current` `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — components/actions/crm/AddToWorkflow.vue:256-281]`.

`fields_referenced: ["workflow_id"]`.
cards.notes:
- **All four modes proven live** `[proven-live 2026-09-26/28]` (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-B-semantics.json`): each contact was parked in a 30-day-wait workflow, then enrolled in a remover whose next step adds a tag. `another` (`workflow_id:[park]`) → the park enrolment ended `finished`, and the remover's next step RAN. `all_except_current` (`allWorkflows:true, includeCurrent:false`) → park ended, next step RAN. `all` (`allWorkflows:true, includeCurrent:true`) → park ended and the remover's next step did NOT run (it removed itself). `current` (`workflow_id:[<its own id>]`, 2026-09-28) → the remover's next step did NOT run and the contact's OTHER enrolment (the park) stayed in `wait_time`: it removes the contact from this workflow only `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3A-crm-basics.json`. (The 2026-09-26 "current" specimen had kept the park id — an edit that did not apply — so it tested `another` twice.)
- `allWorkflows` reaches EVERY workflow the contact is in on the location — including other people's published workflows the contact entered by their own triggers (seen live: a run-created contact had been auto-enrolled by an unrelated published workflow and was removed from it too).
- **`workflow_id` is polymorphic.** Corpus has both `"uuid-string"` and `["uuid-string"]` forms. The TS interface declares `string | string[]`. Either should work; arrays are more recent.
- **The `includeCurrent` key means "all workflows", whatever its value.** The validator skips the `workflow_id` check when the key is present (`internal-action-validators.ts:41-45`), and the builder's constructor sets `allWorkflows = true` whenever `includeCurrent` is defined `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/RemoveFromWorkflow.ts:29-31]`. So `includeCurrent` alone is NOT a "current workflow only" shape: on reopen the builder turns it into an "all workflows" mode. To remove from the current workflow only, store `workflow_id: ["<this workflow's id>"]` with no `includeCurrent` key.
- **`allWorkflows: true` removes from every workflow on the location** — wide blast radius. `includeCurrent: true` also removes the contact from the current workflow (which then halts execution); `includeCurrent: false` spares it.
- **No existence check** on `workflow_id` values. Bogus UUIDs publish cleanly.
- The mirror action is [`add_to_workflow`](./add_to_workflow.md).

cards.title: router
cards.summary: Multi-branch step that sends the contact down **every** branch whose conditions match, one branch after another, left to right. Unlike `if_else` it does not stop at the first match. Beta: hidden from the action picker unless the session is on staging / internal GHL or an allowlisted agency or locati

meta.Validator: No per-action validator key. Router rules run in the workflow-level publish check `validateRouterConditions` and in the drawer's Save [source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/WorkflowValidator.ts:846-890; models/conditions/router-rules.ts:223-247]
meta.Hybrid / multi-path?: Multi-path container. The root node has `type: 'router'`, `nodeType: 'condition-node'`, and `next` = the array of branch ids; each branch is a lane node with `type: 'router'`, `nodeType: 'branch-yes'`, `attributes: {routerBranch: true}`, `parent`/`parentKey` = the router id, `sibling[]` = the other lanes [source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/router.ts:55,70,615-640,653-663,727,763]
meta.Premium / beta?: Beta. `IS_ROUTER_ACTION_SHIPPED = false`; available when `isLocationFlagEnabled` passes (staging / internal GHL, an allowlisted agency — the list is empty — or one of 27 allowlisted locations). Existing router steps still open when the picker hides it [source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/router-flag.ts:9,16,24-52,67-75; utils/workflows.ts:1369-1371]

fields.name: routerName
fields.notes: Node label. Non-empty after trim; within the standard name length limit ("less than 100 characters").

fields.name: branches
fields.notes: Evaluated left to right. At most 10.

cards.validator:
The same rules gate the drawer's Save and publish (`validateRouterBranches`, checked in this order) [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/conditions/router-rules.ts:23,81-86,120-157,172-176,223-230; utils/WorkflowValidator.ts:859-887; utils/router.ts:249,407-415]:

1. `routerName` empty → "Action name cannot be empty!"; too long → length error (drawer only).
2. More than 10 branches → `tooManyBranches`.
3. More than one `fallback` → `fallbackExists`; any `always_run` together with a `fallback` → `alwaysRunFallbackConflict` ("the fallback path will never be run").
4. A branch with no complete condition (custom) → `branchError` naming the branch.
5. Two branches with the same conditions → `duplicateBranchError` ("{name} has the same conditions as {other}").
6. Publish only: a router nested under more than 10 router roots → "Cannot nest more than 10 routers".
7. Publish only: a `workflow_goal` or `goto` step anywhere inside a router branch → "{stepName} cannot be added inside a router branch".
cards.notes:
- **Not an if/else.** Every matching branch runs, left to right ("Send the contact down every branch whose conditions match. Branches run one after another, Left to right") [source-derived 2026-09-26 — i18n `workflow.asideSection.description.router`; models/conditions/router-rules.ts:167-170]. That is why duplicate conditions are refused.
- **`always_run` and `fallback` cannot coexist**; at most one `fallback`.
- **No Goal or Go To inside a branch**, and no more than 10 nested routers.
- **Stamp `nodeType: 'condition-node'` on the root.** Routers added through the builder's generic path were saved without it; the builder repairs that on load (`normalizeRouterTemplates`), and an unstamped router is read as one of its own lanes [source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/router.ts:642-663].
- **Beta-gated.** On an account outside the allowlist the picker hides Router; whether GHL's server accepts a router written by API on such an account is untested. The designated test sub-account is on neither the router nor the loop allowlist (0 hits for its id across the recovered source, the index bundle and every lazy chunk of `bundle-2026-09-29-2`), so router authoring cannot be proven there.
- **The plugin does not author a router.** Its engine refuses one by name (`ROUTER_NOT_AUTHORED`) before anything is written: before 2026-09-29 it compiled an authored router into ONE step with a scalar `next` and no lanes, which saved and validated clean and could not branch [proven-live 2026-09-29 — refusal returned, nothing written: `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/W23-LIVE-PROOFS.md` row 3]. Use `if_else`, or add the Router in the builder where it is offered; an edit leaves an existing router as stored.
- Allowed in object-based (Company / Custom Object) workflows [source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/workflows.ts:1684-1686].

cards.summary: Fires on a cron-like schedule (hourly / daily / weekly / monthly / cron).

conditions.label: Interval
conditions.options: `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`, `cron`

conditions.label: Every (hours)
conditions.options: hourly only; integer 1–255

conditions.label: At what time
conditions.options: daily only; `HH:MM` on a 15-minute grid (`00:00` … `23:45`)

conditions.label: On days
conditions.options: weekly; `monday` … `sunday`

conditions.label: At what time
conditions.options: weekly; 15-minute grid

conditions.label: Pattern
conditions.options: monthly; `dayOfMonth` | `nthWeekday`

conditions.label: On days
conditions.options: monthly + `dayOfMonth`; `'1'` … `'31'` (strings)

conditions.label: Week
conditions.options: monthly + `nthWeekday`; `'1'` … `'4'` (strings)

conditions.label: Day of week
conditions.options: monthly + `nthWeekday`; `monday` … `sunday`

conditions.label: At what time
conditions.options: monthly (both patterns); 15-minute grid

conditions.label: Cron expression
conditions.options: cron only; see Notes for the refused expressions

cards.validator:
`schedulerValidator` checks the following fields (warning-level results) per `sniffs/bundle/trigger-validators-summary.json::schedulerValidator`:

- `scheduler.interval`

All other fields and the body envelope pass without validator inspection. A trigger with no filters is accepted at create time. A filter row with no value is accepted by the API too, but the builder blocks SAVING a trigger that carries one (`TriggerMain.hasErrors` → `checkForEmptyFilter`, `TriggerMain.ts:306-360`; exempt: operator `has-changed`, `has_value`, `has_no_value`, and a value of `false` or `0`) `[source-derived]` — the publish flow uses the same validator chain (`docs/08-validators.md`).
cards.notes:
- `requiresInternalAccess: true` — listed only for internal-staff users in the picker; regular users won't see it. Whether the server enforces this on create has not been tested.
- Every scheduler setting is a row in `conditions[]` (see the table). Monthly uses `scheduler.monthly.patternType` (not `scheduler.monthly.pattern`): `dayOfMonth` adds `monthly.days` + `monthly.times`; `nthWeekday` adds `monthly.weekIndex` + `monthly.weekday` + `monthly.times`. `scheduler.hourly.every` must be an integer from 1 to 255 — the class also has a `validateHourlyInterval` capping at 168, but nothing calls it. A cron expression the builder refuses as high-frequency (runs more than once an hour): minute field `*`, a minute list (`0,30`), a minute step under 60 (`*/15`), or a minute range (`0-30`). An hour step such as `0 */2 * * *` is allowed. [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/Triggers/Filters/SchedulerTriggerFilter.ts:15-31, 40-60, 383-399, 464-476, 552-708; utils/cron-validation.ts:11-67]
- Server-managed: each scheduler trigger gets a `schedule_runtime.task_ref` (queue + name + EXEC type) returned on read. Don't send `schedule_runtime` on create — the server manages it.

Because this asset carries `workflowsTriggerType: "INTERNAL"`, picking it sets `masterType: "internal"` and save stamps `workflowsTriggerType: "INTERNAL"` on the trigger. (An asset without a `workflowsTriggerType` gets `masterType: "marketplace"` and save stamps its `version` + `templateId` instead.) Save also writes `testResponse`, and `integrationAccountId` when one is set. [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/Triggers/TriggerMain.ts:565-573, 907-908, 921-929]

cards.validator:
Two-link delegation per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json`:

```
sendSmsActionValidator(n) → baseSmsValidator(n, translate("sms_body_required"))
```

`baseSmsValidator` logic:

1. If `template_id` is set and not `"none"` → push `{ field: "template_id", resource: "sms_template", value: template_id }` (template-existence lookup).
2. Else if no `attachments` and no `urlAttachments` and `parseHTMLToBody(body)` is empty/whitespace → push `{ field: "body", message: "sms_body_required" }`.
3. Else if `body` has invalid Handlebars → push `{ field: "body", message: "issueInCustomVariables" }`.

Per `sniffs/bundle/validators-summary.json::baseSmsValidator`: `fields_referenced: ["body", "template_id"]`, result level `warning`.

`sendSmsActionValidator` itself is length 76 — just a curry of `baseSmsValidator` with the body-required message. The shared validator is used for `manual-sms` and the SMS branch of `internal_notification` as well.
cards.notes:
- **No phone → skipped, the run continues** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3I-sends.json`: `status: skipped`, `skippedFor: {type: "missing-data", msg: "No Phone number"}`. (The sandbox has no SMS number provisioned, so a delivered SMS is not provable there.) - **"None" in the Templates picker clears the template.** Choosing it deletes `template_id` and brings back an empty Message editor (the template choice had already deleted `body`); `"none"` itself is never stored by the drawer `[source-derived — models/actions/SMS.ts:304-320]`. - **Body is HTML-encoded in the UI but stored as plain text on save** (per `SMS.ts::save` calling `parseHTMLToBody`). A roundtrip through the UI strips HTML tags; if you hand-write `

...

` in `body`, the validator strips the tags only for its empty-body check; `sms` has no length check (only `instagram-dm` has one, 1000 characters). - **No attachment size limit; some file types are filtered.** The builder's size check always passes ("Removed limit on 6th June 2023"); files whose MIME type contains `html`, `php`, `zip` or `rar` are dropped when attached, and for `instagram-dm` only images are kept `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/actions/SMS.ts:272-284,322-326; utils/generalFunctions.ts:271-275]`. The Message editor shows a "{n} characters | {m} words" counter with no maximum `[proven-live 2026-09-30 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-W37-walk-sms-main.json]`, and no segment counter: there is no segment logic in `SendSMS.vue`, `SMS.ts` or anywhere in the recovered source `[source-derived 2026-09-26]`. - **Attachments bypass body**. An SMS with `attachments: [{url, name}]` and empty `body` is publishable. - **Instagram DM uses the same class** with `typeOfMessage: "instagram-dm"` and a 1000-char limit on `body`. The `sms` type is the SMS-specific instance; `messenger`, `gmb`, `instagram-dm` and `manual-sms` reuse the model and drawer under their own types. `whatsapp` has its own model (`models/actions/WhatsApp.ts`). - **`isInternalSMS` flag** is set on the model only when the SMS is nested in an `internal_notification`. This affects which getters validate `to` / `selectedUser`. - The validator is shared with `manual-sms` via the same `baseSmsValidator`. - **`template_id` wins over `body` at runtime.** A step storing body "…BODY-WINS" and a saved snippet's `template_id` recorded a message carrying the SNIPPET's text, merge tags rendered [proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3U3-sms-template-differential.json]. The drawer cannot produce this pair: choosing a template deletes `body` (and `attachments`, `urlAttachments`) and hides the Message editor, so a step storing both was written by the API `[source-derived — models/actions/SMS.ts:304-320; SendSMSMessageForm.vue:22-83]`. The plugin warns `SMS_TEMPLATE_OVERRIDES_BODY`. - **What a run does on a sub-account with no SMS number** (contact with a phone): the step logs `success` with a `conversationId` + `messageId`; the message is recorded outbound with status `failed` and error "Failed: No numbers available in the account. Buy a number to send SMS." Body merge tags render; `urlAttachments` and stored-file `attachments` (`{name, url}`) both appear as the message's `attachments` URLs [proven-live 2026-09-28 — sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3U-messaging-phone.json, live-3U5-sms-stored-attachment.json]. With no phone on the contact it is skipped instead (`missing-data`).

cards.validator:
`stripeOneTimeChargeValidator` (per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json`):

- `amount` set and non-empty, else `amount_required`.
- If `amount` doesn't start with `{{`, must parse as a positive float, else `amount_must_be_positive`.
- `currency` set and non-empty, else `currency_required`.
- `stripe_customer_id` set and non-empty, else `stripe_customer_id_required`.
- `description` not validated despite being marked required in the TS interface — drift between interface and validator.

Per `validators-summary.json`: 3 fields referenced; result level `warning`.
cards.notes:
- 🔴 **Runtime UNPROVEN — needs a connected Stripe account on the sandbox; third-party integrations are out of scope (coordinator 2026-09-28); never run, not even as a no-account probe (coordinator).** `[blocked 2026-09-28]` What IS proven: our build stores it as a DRAFT and it reads back unchanged (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3O3-blocked-drafts.json`), with the fields the builder/GHL require: `amount`, `currency`, `stripe_customer_id`, `description`. Whether it runs, what it sends and what it skips is not known.
- `amount` is a string, not a number — the validator parses it. The handlebar-prefix check (`startsWith("{{")`) is the runtime escape hatch for dynamic amounts.
- Currency is uppercase ISO-4217 per Stripe convention; the validator doesn't enforce format.
- `stripe_customer_id` must resolve to a real Stripe customer on the location's connected account — runtime constraint, not pre-flight.
- Charge failures (declined card, insufficient funds) surface in the workflow context per Stripe webhook responses — handling is downstream concern.

cards.title: task-notification
cards.summary: Create a task assigned to a user, due relative to "now" or a fixed time. Note: registry exposes neither `task_notification` nor `task-notification` — the corpus uses both. Step row's `type` value is `task-notification` (with hyphen); inner `attributes.type` is `task_notification` (with underscore).

meta.UI editor source: No recovered model — the `Notification.ts` model handles in-app notifications, tasks live in a separate component

fields.name: type
fields.notes: Inner type (underscore form). Top-level step `type` is `"task-notification"` (hyphen). 100%.

fields.name: title
fields.notes: Task title. Handlebars supported. 100% of corpus.

fields.name: assignedTo
fields.notes: User id, or `"contact.assigned_user"` sentinel to use the contact's assigned user. 100%.

cards.validator: **None.** `validator: null`, no entry in `validators.json`. Publish accepts any shape. The runtime presumably has its own checks; failure surfaces at task creation.
cards.notes:
- **Type name has a hyphen at the step level and an underscore inside `attributes`.** This is corpus-observed and likely a registration legacy issue. Don't normalize either form — use `type: "task-notification"` at the step row and `attributes.type: "task_notification"` if you set it.
- **`dueDate` polymorphism is the biggest gotcha.** The object form is the modern shape; the integer is a legacy "days from now" shorthand; `"now"` is a special-cased string. Mixing shapes within one workflow is fine; the runtime accepts all three.
- **`dueDate.time` is a snapshot timestamp** captured by the UI when the action was saved (Unix ms). The runtime appears to ignore this in favor of recomputing from `duration` + `unit` — but corpus consistently carries it, so include it for safety.
- **`skipWeekends: true`** in the object form moves the due date past Saturday/Sunday. Behavior on holidays isn't traced.
- **`assignedTo`** accepts a user id string, or the literal `"contact.assigned_user"` to delegate to the contact's owner. Other sentinels haven't been observed.
- **`body` is HTML**. Renders in the task UI. Plain text also works.

### Editor drawer — `task-notification` `[proven-live 2026-09-30]`

A draft built by `build_workflow` (`marketplace: true`, `type: task-notification`, the asset's required inputs authored; `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-W32-mstep-triage-am-add-lead.json`) was opened in the builder and the step card clicked, every write blocked and nothing saved (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-W33-step-task_notification.json`). Card: "task-notification". The drawer shows, after *Action name*: no further control. Inputs the asset declares as dynamic are filled in by the drawer's own read-only `dynamic-fields` / `branches` / `dynamic-source` calls, which the guarded run allowed (they only read).

cards.title: transition
cards.summary: Internal bookkeeping row that represents a branch's "outbound edge label" on multi-path parents. Not user-authored — created and maintained by the builder.

meta.Validator: None of its own; the publish validator checks a branching `wait`'s transitions (see Validator)
meta.Hybrid / multi-path?: Multi-path bookkeeping (lives as a child under a multi-path parent's branch)
meta.UI editor source: No drawer and no model class — the parent's drawer writes the rows on save (`wait`, `find_contact`, `workflow_split`, internal/marketplace multipath such as `find_opportunity`, `ivr_gather`, Conversation AI, interactive messenger). If/Else branches are not transitions.

fields.name: type
fields.notes: Written by the parent drawer: `wait_condition`, `wait_reply`, `wait_link_clicked`, `wait_email_event`, `wait_user_replied` (primary wait branch), `wait_timeout`, `contact_found`, `contact_not_found`; `workflow_split` writes none. 34.2%.

fields.name: description
fields.notes: Branch description written by the parent drawer: Find Contact writes the translated `Contact found` / `Contact not found` (English); a wait branch carries its wait type's sentence. 34.2%.

cards.validator:
**None of its own.** The string `"transition"` is not registered in `sniffs/bundle/registry-parsed.json::entries[]`. No `transitionValidator` exists in `sniffs/bundle/validators.json`. The builder's publish validator does check a branching `wait`'s transitions and blocks publish (severity `error`) when the wait has fewer than 2 transitions or lists a transition id missing from the workflow — errors quoted under Builder options and limits `[source-derived — utils/WorkflowValidator.ts:917-966]`.

A `transition` row's own contents are not checked: it passes publish whatever its `name` or `attributes`, provided the parent multi-path node references its id in `parentKey` and `transitions[]` / `next[]`.
cards.notes:
- **Do not author this manually unless mirroring corpus.** The builder (client side) writes the `transition` rows when a multi-path parent's drawer (e.g. `find_contact`, `find_opportunity`, `workflow_split`) is saved, and sets the parent's `next` to their ids. Each branch outcome becomes one `transition` child carrying the branch name as `name`.
- **`attributes` depends on the parent.** `workflow_split` writes `{}`; `wait` and `find_contact` write `type` + `description` (see Attributes shape). The row carries `parentKey` (plus `parent` from the WorkflowTreeV2 canvas only) pointing to the multi-path parent and `name` carrying the branch label.
- **The 269 corpus occurrences** correspond mostly to `find_contact` (`Contact Found` / `Contact Not Found`) and `find_opportunity` (`Opportunity Found` / `Opportunity Not Found`) auto-generated rows.
- **`type` (inside attributes) is informational only**: values like `contact_found` / `wait_reply` echo the parent's branch outcome but are not consumed by the runtime as discriminators.
- For the full multi-path graph picture see [`docs/04-workflow-anatomy.md §4`](../../10-anatomy/04-workflow-anatomy.md).

cards.validator:
`updateContactFieldValidator` (length 680, result level `warning`). Per `sniffs/bundle/validators.json::updateContactFieldValidator`:

1. If `attributes.fields` is missing or empty → push `{ field: "fields", message: "at_least_one_field_required" }`.
2. For each entry in `fields[]`:
   - If `field` is not in `contactStandardFields` → push `{ field: <field>, resource: "custom_field" }` to trigger a custom-field-existence lookup against the location.
   - If `actionType` is `"update_field_data"` or `"add_field_data"` and the value is missing (`null`/`""`/empty array; `false` and `0` count as present; `date: "currentDate"` exempts it) → push `{ field: <field>, message: missing_value_for_field }` `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/validators/contact-action-validators.ts:12-18,44-75]`.

So a publishable step requires:

- `actionType: "update_field_data"` or `"add_field_data"` with at least one `fields[]` entry whose `value` is present (or `date: "currentDate"`); OR
- `actionType: "clear_field_data"` with at least one `fields[]` entry (value can be empty).
cards.notes:
- **`add_field_data` appends on a CHECKBOX field too; `update_field_data` replaces** `[proven-live 2026-09-29]`: an own CHECKBOX field seeded `["a"]` read back `["a","b"]` after an add of `["b"]`, then `["c"]` after an update of `["c"]`. The row's type hint is `multiselect`, as for MULTIPLE_OPTIONS (`utils/conditions.ts:494-496`) (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-W25-checkbox-add.json`).
- 🔴 **A multi-option field's `type` hint must be `multiselect`** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]`: `type: "array"` was refused by GHL's validator at save — "textbox_list takes a string or an object of string values; multiselect takes a string or an array of strings/numbers; every other type takes a string or a number" (`live-3B-fields-math-run1-multiselect-type.json`).
- **All three `actionType`s and all three date modes run** `[proven-live 2026-09-28]` `sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-3B-fields-math.json`: `update_field_data` wrote NUMERICAL `10`, MONETORY `100.5`, TEXT, MULTIPLE_OPTIONS `["a"]`, DATE `specificDate` `2026-01-31`, DATE `currentDate` (the run's date); `add_field_data` on the MULTIPLE_OPTIONS field turned `["a"]` into `["a","b"]`; `customDate` `03-15-2026` stored `2026-03-15`; `clear_field_data` emptied a NUMERICAL and a MULTIPLE_OPTIONS field (read back `null`). Custom fields are addressed by field ID.
- **Standard vs custom is decided by the key.** A key in the builder's `contactStandardFields` list (camelCase — see the `field` row) is a standard field; anything else is treated as a custom-field id and checked to exist. A snake_case key such as `first_name` is NOT a standard key. Proof: 2026-09-25, `firstName: "WaveOneFirst"` and `companyName: "WaveOneCo"` written by a live run and read back on the contact (`sniffs/workflows-wave1-2026-09-25/live-A-formatters.json`) `[proven-live 2026-09-25]`.
- **Clearing requires the field id in `fields[]`** with empty `value`. Sending `actionType: "clear_field_data"` with `fields: []` still trips the empty-array warning.
- **Clear mode cannot clear `country`, `timezone`, `firstName` or `dnd`** — the builder drops them from the clear picker (`excludeFromClearFields`); the clear picker does offer Contact ID (`id`), which the update picker omits `[source-derived 2026-09-30 — utils/ContactFieldEditing.ts:20,228-246]`.
- **FILE_UPLOAD custom fields can only be cleared, not written** — the update picker filters them out; only the clear picker lists them `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/ContactFieldEditing.ts:200-204]`.
- **`dnd` is a true/false select ("Enable DND for all channels" / "Disable DND for all channels") and is selectable in the Update picker**: the catalogue marks it disabled, but `filterFieldOptions()` overwrites `isDisabled` with "already used", so only the info tooltip "Please use the Enable/Disable DND Action instead." remains — the builder points to `dnd_contact` for DND `[source-derived 2026-09-30 — utils/ContactFieldEditing.ts:137-155; models/actions/ContactField.ts:170-180]` `[ASSUMPTION — clickable live not yet walked; from ContactField.ts:174-176 overriding ContactFieldEditing.ts:153]`. **`timezone` is an enum select** over the builder's timezone list `[source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/ContactFieldEditing.ts:157-166]`.
- **`title` is UI-only** — don't rely on it. The runtime resolves by `field` id alone.
- **`date: "currentDate"` is a sentinel** that means "use the current date at execution time" — bypasses the value-required check.
- **`value`'s type hint (`"numerical"`, `"date"`, etc.)** affects how the value is parsed at execution; mismatches haven't been exhaustively tested but corpus shows numeric values stored as JSON numbers when `type: "numerical"`.
- This step only writes to the workflow's running contact. To write to a different contact, use `create_update_contact` (separate type).

cards.summary: Pause execution until a time elapses, a condition becomes true, an event fires, or a reply arrives — discriminated by `attributes.type`.

meta.Validator: `waitValidator` (dispatches its 13 types to 9 sub-validators by `attributes.type`, plus `validateTimeout`)
meta.Hybrid / multi-path?: Hybrid — runs linear by default, becomes multi-path when `convertToMultipath: true`. Branching is allowed only for `type` `condition`, `reply`, `link_clicked`, `email_event`, `user_replied`; a branching wait needs an array `next` with at least 2 entries, and every transition id must exist as a template. Anything else is a blocking publish error [source-derived 2026-09-26 — utils/WorkflowValidator.ts:925-968]. Carries `isHybridAction: true` and `hybridActionType: "wait"` markers. See [`docs/04-workflow-anatomy.md §4`](../../10-anatomy/04-workflow-anatomy.md)

fields.name: type
fields.notes: Discriminator, THIRTEEN values: `"time" | "condition" | "reply" | "appointment" | "service_booking" | "rental_booking" | "attendee_event_date" | "overdue" | "email_event" | "link_clicked" | "user_replied" | "specific_date" | "recurring_schedule"`. 🔴 This row listed EIGHT until 2026-09-16 — the eight with corpus instances, not the ones GHL accepts; `waitValidator` dispatches on all thirteen. Engine support: the compiler authors `specific_date` in full (its own checks). It has no dedicated builder for `recurring_schedule`, `user_replied`, `rental_booking` or `attendee_event_date`: their attributes pass through and are stored as written (`recurring_schedule` proven that way, 3C/3AL), with nothing checking them before GHL does. See the sub-validator table for each one's required fields.

fields.name: name
fields.notes: Required when populated; max length capped by `isWithinLimits`. 94.2%.

fields.name: startAfter
fields.notes: `{ type: "seconds" | "minutes" | "hour" | "days", value: number, when: "after" | ... }`. Required for `time`. 90.7%. The drawer's unit VALUES are `seconds`, `minutes`, `hour` (singular) and `days` — `startAfterTypeOptions` (Wait.ts:1588, bundle-2026-08-21-3) maps the plural LABEL "hours" to the value `hour`. The TS interface still declares `'minutes' | 'hours' | 'days'`, and stored workflows contain both spellings (`startAfter` blocks in corpus+sniffs: minutes ×71, days ×10, hours ×4, hour ×1) — so a stored `hours` was written by an API call, not the drawer. Whether the scheduler honours it is UNPROVEN; the engine accepts it with a warning.

fields.name: specificDatePassed
fields.notes: `"next" | "exit" | "specific_step" | "skip"` — what happens when a `specific_date` wait's date is ALREADY PAST. Drawer: *If this date has already passed*. `next` = Continue to next action (released immediately, fails LOUD); `exit` = Exit contact from automation; `skip` = **Skip all outbound communication actions till next wait or event start date action** (hint "Email, SMS, call & voicemail"; proceeds with messages SUPPRESSED, fails SILENT) — note this is NOT "skip the step", the contact still advances; `specific_step` = Go to specific step, and the validator refuses without `specificDateStep`. 🔴 The default is `skip`, the SILENT one: author `"next"` explicitly if a stale date should be visible. 🔴 The drawer's radio falls back to `next` for DISPLAY when the key is absent, while the drawer writes `skip` when the specific-date type is first chosen (`setInitialSpecificDate`) — an API step that omits it reads in the builder as something it is not, so always write the key.

fields.name: specificDateProceed
fields.notes: `"on" | "before" | "after"` — the drawer's three radios "On this date and time" / "Before this date" / "After this date". `on` and `after` passed `validate_workflow` in a live probe on 2026-09-16, with a nonsense control refused naming the field and value. If `before`/`after`, at least one of `specificDateOffsetDays/Hours/Minutes` must be non-zero.

fields.name: appointmentStartAfter
fields.notes: `{ when: "now" | "before" | "after", type, value, distributed }`. Required for `appointment` / `service_booking` / `rental_booking` / `attendee_event_date` / `overdue`. `distributed` is the drawer's `{months, days, hours, minutes}` offset breakdown, clamped to 9999 / 30 / 23 / 59. On save (appointment, overdue, service_booking, rental_booking, attendee_event_date) it collapses into `type: "minutes"` and `value` = the total minutes. With `when` `before`/`after` the offset must be non-zero [source-derived 2026-09-26 — models/conditions/Wait.ts:1025-1036,1106-1112,1395-1420; models/Workflow.ts:680-709]. 9.3%.

fields.name: appointmentCondition
fields.notes: `skip | next | specific-step | exit`: what to do when the target time has ALREADY PASSED (for example a "1 day before" wait on an appointment booked less than 24 h out). `specific-step` jumps straight to `appointmentSpecificStep`, skipping everything between: the log row reads `status: "wait_finished"`, `skippedFor: {type: "appointment-wait", msg: "Appointment wait time was in the past (…).
